ontologyNodes.definition: Analogous to savour but operating through air and water; divided into two species: nutritive odours correlated with savours (shared by all animals) and odours pleasant in their essential nature (perceived only by humans).

ontologyNodes.name: τὰ ἴδια αἰσθητά
ontologyNodes.definition: Objects specific to each sense (colour to sight, sound to hearing, etc.); the senses are not deceived about their proper objects; contrasted with common sensibles.

ontologyNodes.name: μέγεθος
ontologyNodes.definition: Every sensible object is a magnitude; the distance from which it can be perceived is determinate, with an indivisible boundary between imperceptibility and perceptibility.

ontologyNodes.name: παράθεσις
ontologyNodes.definition: Side-by-side placement of white and black in imperceptibly small quantities; rejected hypothesis for intermediate colour generation.

ontologyNodes.name: τὸ ὑγρόν
ontologyNodes.definition: The material substrate in which savour is generated; water as the base medium for taste, analogous to the transparent for colour.

ontologyNodes.name: σκότος
ontologyNodes.definition: The privation of light; the condition of the transparent when the fiery element is absent.

ontologyNodes.name: Being
ontologyNodes.definition: The fundamental theme of the treatise — not a being (Seiendes) but that which determines beings as beings. The question of the meaning of Being (Sinn von Sein) drives the entire inquiry. Not a genus, not definable through traditional logic, yet pre-ontologically understood by Dasein in every comportment toward beings.

ontologyNodes.name: Being-in-the-world
ontologyNodes.definition: The unitary, a priori structural whole that constitutes Dasein's basic state. Not a spatial containment but a mode of existing: Dasein is always already "in" a world, engaged with entities, alongside others. Its three structural moments — Being-in, world, the who — are analyzed in Division One and temporally grounded in Division Two.

ontologyNodes.name: Care
ontologyNodes.definition: The structural totality of Dasein's Being, formally articulated as Being-ahead-of-itself-already-in-(the-world)-alongside (entities encountered within-the-world). Unifies the existential moments of existence (understanding/projection), facticity (thrownness/state-of-mind), and falling. Demonstrated through the phenomenon of anxiety, confirmed by the cura fable, and temporally grounded as the meaning of temporality.

ontologyNodes.name: Temporality
ontologyNodes.definition: The ontological meaning of care and the primordial horizon for the understanding of Being. Unfolds in three ecstases — future (Zukunft), having-been (Gewesenheit), Present (Gegenwart) — each with an authentic and inauthentic mode. Temporality is not a sequence of "nows" but the ecstatic-horizonal unity that makes possible Dasein's existence, facticity, and falling. Distinguished from Temporalität (temporality of Being as such), which B&T announces but does not fully develop.

ontologyNodes.name: Being-towards-death
ontologyNodes.definition: Dasein's ownmost, non-relational, not-to-be-outstripped, certain yet indefinite possibility. Death is not an event at the end of life but the possibility of the impossibility of existence — a constitutive structure that individualizes Dasein and opens authentic self-understanding. Anticipation (Vorlaufen) lets Dasein hold open this possibility without fleeing into the "they's" evasive interpretations.

ontologyNodes.name: Disclosedness
ontologyNodes.definition: The "there" (Da) of Dasein — the clearing in which entities can show themselves and Dasein can encounter itself. Equiprimordially constituted by state-of-mind, understanding, and discourse. Disclosedness is more primordial than any propositional truth; it is the existential-ontological condition for truth as unconcealment. Falling both belongs to and conceals this disclosedness.

ontologyNodes.name: Understanding
ontologyNodes.definition: An equiprimordial existentiale of disclosedness (alongside state-of-mind and discourse). Understanding is Dasein's projective grasp of its own potentiality-for-Being and of the Being of entities it encounters. Always has the structure of projection (Entwurf) and discloses possibilities, not merely cognitive contents. Developed in interpretation (Auslegung), which articulates the fore-structure. Temporally grounded in the ecstasis of the future.

ontologyNodes.name: State-of-mind
ontologyNodes.definition: An equiprimordial existentiale of disclosedness that discloses Dasein's thrownness and facticity. Ontically manifested as mood (Stimmung). Every state-of-mind discloses Dasein as already delivered over to its "there" — it reveals the "that it is" while the "whence and whither" remain in darkness. Fear is an inauthentic mode; anxiety is the fundamental mode that discloses Being-in-the-world as such. Temporally grounded in having-been.

ontologyNodes.name: Falling
ontologyNodes.definition: Dasein's tendency to lose itself in the "they" and in the entities it encounters within-the-world. Not a moral failing or a Fall from a higher state but an essential existential structure: Dasein is proximally and for the most part absorbed in its world. Manifested concretely as idle talk, curiosity, and ambiguity. Characterized by temptation, tranquillizing, alienation, and entanglement (downward plunge). Temporally grounded in inauthentic making-present.

ontologyNodes.name: Resoluteness
ontologyNodes.definition: BT §60 existential structure. Gross-B: BT 344 'only authentically Being-their-Selves in resoluteness can people authentically be with one another' — but this BT-confinement (HR-01-GROSS-B-P8) is the depoliticization move. Hyde: the call of conscience summons resoluteness; 'ethics emerges as responsibility of affirming our freedom through resolute choice.' Kisiel: Heidegger's framework translates Aristotelian ethos into Entschlossenheit (the politician/speaker's resoluteness brings others to same resolution = kairos). SZ 384 'communication and struggle' (Mitteilung und Kampf) as path out of leveling Anyone.
ontologyNodes.text: Heidegger - Being and Time; Heidegger and Rhetoric

ontologyNodes.name: Worldhood
ontologyNodes.definition: The ontological structure of the world as an existentiale of Dasein, analyzed through the referential totality of significance (Bedeutsamkeit). Not the totality of beings but the relational context (involvement, for-the-sake-of-which) within which entities can be encountered as ready-to-hand. Temporally grounded in the horizonal schema of the ecstases.

ontologyNodes.name: Readiness-to-hand
ontologyNodes.definition: The mode of Being of equipment (Zeug) as encountered in circumspective concern. Equipment is not first perceived as an object with properties (presence-at-hand) and then given a value-predicate; rather, it is encountered as something in-order-to, within a totality of involvements. Readiness-to-hand is ontologically prior to presence-at-hand.

ontologyNodes.name: Presence-at-hand
ontologyNodes.definition: The mode of Being of entities as they show themselves when circumspective concern breaks down or when theoretical attitude takes over. The present-at-hand is an entity stripped of its involvement-character, regarded as a mere "thing" with determinate properties. Traditional ontology (Descartes, the metaphysical tradition) privileges this mode, mistakenly taking it as the primary way of Being.

ontologyNodes.name: Authenticity/Inauthenticity
ontologyNodes.definition: The two fundamental modes in which Dasein can be itself. Authenticity: Dasein owns its existence, projecting upon its ownmost possibilities. Inauthenticity: Dasein disperses itself in the "they," evading its ownmost Being. Both are genuine modes of existence — inauthenticity is not lesser but the proximal and average way Dasein exists. The distinction runs through every existential structure.

ontologyNodes.name: Anxiety
ontologyNodes.definition: The fundamental state-of-mind that discloses Dasein's Being-in-the-world as such. Distinguished from fear: fear has a definite within-the-world object, anxiety does not. In anxiety, the world sinks into insignificance, the "they" collapses, and Dasein is individualized, thrown back upon its ownmost potentiality-for-Being. Reveals the uncanniness (Unheimlichkeit) underlying everydayness. Serves as the methodological access point for the phenomenon of care.

ontologyNodes.name: Conscience
ontologyNodes.definition: The call (Ruf) of care that summons Dasein from its lostness in the "they" to its ownmost Being-guilty. Conscience discloses Dasein's nullity — the constitutive not-Being at the ground of its thrown projection. The caller is Dasein itself in its uncanniness; the called is the they-self. Wanting-to-have-a-conscience is the existentiell choice of resoluteness.

ontologyNodes.name: Discourse
ontologyNodes.definition: The third equiprimordial existentiale of disclosedness (with state-of-mind and understanding). Discourse articulates the intelligibility of Being-in-the-world. It is more primordial than language (Sprache), which is the worldly expression of discourse. Constitutive moments: what discourse is about, what is said, communication, making-known. Includes hearing (Hören) and keeping silent (Schweigen). Falls into idle talk (Gerede) in everydayness.

ontologyNodes.name: Thrownness
ontologyNodes.definition: Dasein's factical character of being delivered over to its "there." Dasein finds itself always already in a world, with a past and possibilities not of its choosing. Thrownness is disclosed in state-of-mind and constitutes the "already-in" moment of care. In Division Two, thrownness is temporally deepened as having-been (Gewesenheit) and ontologically extended through historicality.

ontologyNodes.name: Spatiality
ontologyNodes.definition: Dasein's existential spatiality, constituted by de-severance (Ent-fernung, bringing-close) and directionality (Ausrichtung). Not Cartesian extensio but a mode of Being-in-the-world: Dasein de-severs entities by bringing them into the nearness of concern. Grounded in temporality (the ecstasis of making-present) but not reducible to temporality. Space is neither "in" the subject nor "in" the world but discovered through Dasein's spatial Being-in-the-world.

ontologyNodes.name: Historicality
ontologyNodes.definition: Dasein's ontological constitution as historical, grounded in the ecstatic-horizonal temporality of care. Dasein "historizes" (geschieht): it stretches along between birth and death, inheriting a heritage and projecting possibilities that have-been. Authentic historicality is fate (Schicksal) — resolute taking-over of inherited possibilities. Communal historicality is destiny (Geschick). Founds the possibility of historiology as a science.

ontologyNodes.name: Within-time-ness
ontologyNodes.definition: The most derivative level of temporality: time as publicly encountered "in which" events and entities occur. Characterized by datability, significance, spannedness, and publicness. Expressed through reckoning with time and clock-use. When its existential origins are levelled off, within-time-ness degenerates into the "ordinary" concept of time as an infinite, homogeneous sequence of nows (now-time, Jetzt-Zeit). Aristotle's definition of time as the number of motion belongs here.

ontologyNodes.name: Interpretation
ontologyNodes.definition: The working-out of possibilities projected in understanding. Not a bare cognitive act but the articulation of what is understood through the fore-structure: fore-having (Vorhabe), fore-sight (Vorsicht), fore-conception (Vorgriff). The hermeneutical "as" (something as something) is the primordial "as-structure" of interpretation. The apophantical "as" of assertion (Aussage) is a derivative modification.

ontologyNodes.name: Being-with
ontologyNodes.definition: The existential structure through which Dasein is always already with Others. Not an additive relation (subject + subject) but an a priori co-constitution of Being-in-the-world. Others are encountered "from the world" of shared concern, not as present-at-hand objects. Gives rise to solicitude (Fürsorge) in its positive modes (leaping-in/dominating vs. leaping-ahead/liberating).

ontologyNodes.name: Destruktion
ontologyNodes.definition: The critical dismantling of the traditional concepts of ontology to lay bare the original experiences from which they arose. Not destruction in the negative sense but a positive appropriation that loosens the hardened tradition. Targets Kant, Descartes, Aristotle as stations. Only partially carried out in B&T; announced in the Introduction as the second task of the treatise.
ontologyNodes.text: Heidegger - Being and Time; Heidegger and Rhetoric

ontologyNodes.name: Existence
ontologyNodes.definition: The kind of Being toward which Dasein can comport itself and always does comport itself somehow. Dasein's "essence" lies in its existence — it is what it can be. Distinguished from the traditional existentia (actuality, presence-at-hand of an entity). Existentialia are the Being-characters of Dasein; categories belong to non-Dasein entities.

ontologyNodes.name: Fear
ontologyNodes.definition: An inauthentic mode of state-of-mind with a definite threatening entity (Wovor), a specific threatened entity (Worum), and a particular way of fearing. Distinguished from anxiety, which has no definite within-the-world object. Fear flees from a definite threat; anxiety discloses Being-in-the-world as such.

ontologyNodes.name: Signs
ontologyNodes.definition: A particular kind of equipment whose function is to indicate — to make a referential totality conspicuous. Signs serve circumspection by orienting Dasein within its environment. Analyzed as a case study in the structure of reference (Verweisung) and worldhood.

ontologyNodes.name: Idle talk
ontologyNodes.definition: The everyday mode of discourse in which communication spreads and repeats what is said without genuine appropriation. Language becomes groundless — understanding floats free of the things themselves. One of the three concrete modes of falling (with curiosity and ambiguity).

ontologyNodes.name: Curiosity
ontologyNodes.definition: The everyday mode of seeing that seeks novelty for its own sake, never dwelling but always moving on. A fallen mode of circumspection freed from its practical context. Traced to Aristotle's wonder but shown to be its inauthentic derivative.

ontologyNodes.name: Phenomenology
ontologyNodes.definition: The method of the treatise: "To let that which shows itself be seen from itself in the very way in which it shows itself from itself." Composed of phenomenon (that which shows itself) and logos (letting something be seen). Phenomenology is ontology — access to the question of Being requires the phenomenological method. Hermeneutical in character: an interpretive uncovering.

ontologyNodes.name: Reality
ontologyNodes.definition: Traditionally identified with the Being of entities (res). Heidegger argues Reality is ontologically grounded in care: "Reality" as a mode of Being of within-the-world entities presupposes Being-in-the-world. Neither the independence of the "external world" nor realism vs. idealism can be resolved without first clarifying the Being of the entity that raises such questions. Resistance (Widerständigkeit) reveals Reality in practical coping, not in theoretical perception.

ontologyNodes.name: Circumspection
ontologyNodes.definition: The kind of sight (Sicht) belonging to practical concern with ready-to-hand entities. Not theoretical observation but a looking-around that guides Dasein's handling of equipment. When circumspection encounters breakdown (conspicuousness, obtrusiveness, obstinacy), the ready-to-hand entity begins to show itself as present-at-hand.

ontologyNodes.name: Selfhood
ontologyNodes.definition: The existential-ontological constitution of Dasein's self-constancy (Selbst-ständigkeit). Not a persisting substance (soul, subject, person) but grounded in the ecstatic unity of temporality. Authentic Selfhood: Self-constancy in anticipatory resoluteness. Inauthentic selfhood: the they-self's lack of Self-constancy (un-Selbst-ständigkeit).

ontologyNodes.name: Temporalität
ontologyNodes.definition: The temporality of Being itself — distinguished from Zeitlichkeit (temporality of Dasein). The projected but unfinished horizon of the treatise: B&T demonstrates Zeitlichkeit but only announces Temporalität as the answer to the question of the meaning of Being in general. The unpublished Division Three was to have worked this out. Remains the "open question" of the book.

ontologyNodes.name: πέρας
ontologyNodes.definition: Limit, boundary; a positive being-aspect in beings, not relational; constitutes the genuine there of a being; connected to τέλος, ὁρισμός, and πέρας as site (τόπος).
ontologyNodes.text: Heidegger - Basic Concepts of Aristotelian Philosophy

ontologyNodes.name: πρᾶξις
ontologyNodes.definition: Action, concern; the mode of being proper to human beings; πρακτική τοῦ λόγον ἔχοντος; distinguished from ποίησις by dependence on προαίρεσις.
ontologyNodes.text: Heidegger - Basic Concepts of Aristotelian Philosophy

ontologyNodes.name: τέλος / τέλειον
ontologyNodes.definition: End (as limit, not aim); completedness; τέλειον = a way of being, a mode of being itself; three senses from Met. Δ16.
ontologyNodes.text: Heidegger - Basic Concepts of Aristotelian Philosophy

ontologyNodes.name: στέρησις
ontologyNodes.definition: Privation, not-having; a positive ontological determination -- "negation is a position"; constitutive of being, not a deficiency.
ontologyNodes.text: Heidegger - Basic Concepts of Aristotelian Philosophy

ontologyNodes.name: δόξα
ontologyNodes.definition: Opinion, having-a-view; the basic phenomenon of everydayness; "genuine discoveredness of being-with-one-another-in-the-world"; reaches to πάντα.
ontologyNodes.text: Heidegger - Basic Concepts of Aristotelian Philosophy

ontologyNodes.name: φόβος
ontologyNodes.definition: Fear, being-afraid; a λύπη τις ἢ ταραχή from φαντασία of impending evil; discloses the futural character of being-there; condition of the possibility of courage.
ontologyNodes.text: Heidegger - Basic Concepts of Aristotelian Philosophy

ontologyNodes.name: ὁρισμός
ontologyNodes.definition: Definition, limitation; λόγος οὐσίας; not a scholastic technique but a mode of disclosive speech exhibiting the being of beings.
ontologyNodes.text: Heidegger - Basic Concepts of Aristotelian Philosophy

ontologyNodes.name: κοινωνία
ontologyNodes.definition: Being-with-one-another, community; fulfilled in δόξα; the social context of λόγος and ἀληθεύειν.
ontologyNodes.text: Heidegger - Basic Concepts of Aristotelian Philosophy

ontologyNodes.name: ἡδονή / λύπη
ontologyNodes.definition: Pleasure/pain; fundamental determinations of being-in-the-world; co-given with all πάθη; ground of δίωξις and φυγή.
ontologyNodes.text: Heidegger - Basic Concepts of Aristotelian Philosophy

ontologyNodes.name: ἀληθεύειν / ἀλήθεια
ontologyNodes.definition: Truth-disclosing, being-unconcealed; a ἕξις accomplished in being-in-the-world; five modes in NE Book 6 (σοφία, φρόνησις, etc.).
ontologyNodes.text: Heidegger - Basic Concepts of Aristotelian Philosophy

ontologyNodes.name: καιρός
ontologyNodes.definition: The moment, the decisive moment; the entirety of circumstances; ἀρετή as ἕξις is oriented toward the καιρός; the mean = καιρός.
ontologyNodes.text: Heidegger - Basic Concepts of Aristotelian Philosophy

ontologyNodes.name: φιλοσοφία / διαλεκτική / σοφιστική
ontologyNodes.text: Heidegger - Basic Concepts of Aristotelian Philosophy

ontologyNodes.name: κατηγορήματα
ontologyNodes.text: Heidegger - Basic Concepts of Aristotelian Philosophy

ontologyNodes.name: ζῷον λόγον ἔχον
ontologyNodes.text: Heidegger - Basic Concepts of Aristotelian Philosophy

ontologyNodes.name: πίστις
ontologyNodes.text: Heidegger - Basic Concepts of Aristotelian Philosophy

ontologyNodes.name: ἀπορία
ontologyNodes.text: Heidegger - Basic Concepts of Aristotelian Philosophy

ontologyNodes.name: ποίησις
ontologyNodes.text: Heidegger - Basic Concepts of Aristotelian Philosophy

ontologyNodes.name: φυσικός
ontologyNodes.text: Heidegger - Basic Concepts of Aristotelian Philosophy

ontologyNodes.name: Vorhabe / Vorsicht / Vorgriff
ontologyNodes.text: Heidegger - Basic Concepts of Aristotelian Philosophy

ontologyNodes.name: πρός τι
ontologyNodes.text: Heidegger - Basic Concepts of Aristotelian Philosophy

ontologyNodes.name: Fundamental attunement
ontologyNodes.definition: A mood that discloses beings as a whole and how we stand amid them; the disclosive ground of the whole analysis, awakened rather than ascertained (§16, p.59 / pdf 42).
ontologyNodes.text: Heidegger - The Fundamental Concepts of Metaphysics

ontologyNodes.name: Awakening
ontologyNodes.definition: Letting what is asleep become wakeful; the method by which an attunement is grasped, as against ascertaining something present-at-hand (§16, p.59 / pdf 42).
ontologyNodes.text: Heidegger - The Fundamental Concepts of Metaphysics

ontologyNodes.name: First form of boredom
ontologyNodes.definition: Boredom attached to a determinate culprit (the train-station): we are left empty and held in limbo and fight it openly by passing the time (§§19–23, pp.78–105 / pdf 51–64).
ontologyNodes.text: Heidegger - The Fundamental Concepts of Metaphysics

ontologyNodes.name: Second form of boredom
ontologyNodes.definition: Boredom with no determinate culprit (the dinner-party): outwardly engaged yet bored from out of Dasein itself; occupied surface and empty depth coexist (§§24–28, pp.106–131 / pdf 65–77).
ontologyNodes.text: Heidegger - The Fundamental Concepts of Metaphysics

ontologyNodes.name: Being left empty
ontologyNodes.definition: The telling refusal of beings, which withdraw into indifference and offer nothing; first localized at §23d (p.101 / pdf 62), radicalized at §31a (p.137 / pdf 80).
ontologyNodes.text: Heidegger - The Fundamental Concepts of Metaphysics

ontologyNodes.name: Being held in limbo
ontologyNodes.definition: Time dragging holds us suspended; in profound boredom, being impelled toward what makes Dasein possible (§23c, p.99 / pdf 61; §31b, p.140 / pdf 82).
ontologyNodes.text: Heidegger - The Fundamental Concepts of Metaphysics

ontologyNodes.name: Telling refusal
ontologyNodes.definition: The refusal of beings as a whole that nonetheless announces; the radicalized form of being-left-empty in profound boredom (§31a, p.137 / pdf 80).
ontologyNodes.text: Heidegger - The Fundamental Concepts of Metaphysics

ontologyNodes.name: Passing the time
ontologyNodes.definition: The counter-move that drives boredom off and "drives time on," betraying boredom's temporal heart; concrete in looking at our watch (§23a–b, pp.93–96 / pdf 58–60).
ontologyNodes.text: Heidegger - The Fundamental Concepts of Metaphysics

ontologyNodes.name: Casualness
ontologyNodes.definition: The obstructive casual going-along that, in the second form, is the deepening way we are left empty in a self-formed emptiness (§25b, p.116 / pdf 70).
ontologyNodes.text: Heidegger - The Fundamental Concepts of Metaphysics

ontologyNodes.name: Entrancement
ontologyNodes.definition: Being entranced by the single threefold horizon of time; the temporal character of being-left-empty in profound boredom (§32a, p.145 / pdf 84).
ontologyNodes.text: Heidegger - The Fundamental Concepts of Metaphysics

ontologyNodes.name: Moment of vision
ontologyNodes.definition: That toward which entranced time impels us; the temporal character of being-held-in-limbo, announced but never given as a signal (§32b, p.148 / pdf 86).
ontologyNodes.text: Heidegger - The Fundamental Concepts of Metaphysics

ontologyNodes.name: The standing now
ontologyNodes.definition: Time brought to a stand in boredom; the making-present that holds the time taken at a standstill (§26, p.126 / pdf 74).
ontologyNodes.text: Heidegger - The Fundamental Concepts of Metaphysics

ontologyNodes.name: World
ontologyNodes.definition: The first metaphysical question released by profound boredom; ultimately the manifestness of beings as such as a whole (§39, p.169 / pdf 96; §68, p.282 / pdf 153).
ontologyNodes.text: Heidegger - The Fundamental Concepts of Metaphysics

ontologyNodes.name: Individuation
ontologyNodes.definition: The second metaphysical question released by profound boredom; the singularizing of Dasein (§39, p.169 / pdf 96).
ontologyNodes.text: Heidegger - The Fundamental Concepts of Metaphysics

ontologyNodes.name: Finitude
ontologyNodes.definition: The third metaphysical question released by profound boredom, rooted with the others in the essence of time (§39, p.169 / pdf 96).
ontologyNodes.text: Heidegger - The Fundamental Concepts of Metaphysics

ontologyNodes.name: Worldless
ontologyNodes.definition: The thesis that the stone has no access to beings at all; the lower pole of the comparative triad (§42, p.176 / pdf 100; §47, p.196 / pdf 110).
ontologyNodes.text: Heidegger - The Fundamental Concepts of Metaphysics

ontologyNodes.name: Poor in world
ontologyNodes.definition: The thesis that the animal is deprived of world — a being-open in captivation withheld from beings as beings; poverty as deprivation, not lesser degree (§42, p.176 / pdf 100; §46, p.192 / pdf 108).
ontologyNodes.text: Heidegger - The Fundamental Concepts of Metaphysics

ontologyNodes.name: World-forming
ontologyNodes.definition: The thesis that man forms world by taking beings as beings (the "as"-structure), culminating in projection (§42, p.176 / pdf 100; §76, p.360 / pdf 192).
ontologyNodes.text: Heidegger - The Fundamental Concepts of Metaphysics

ontologyNodes.name: Captivation
ontologyNodes.definition: The animal's absorption in itself; being taken/benumbed such that beings are never manifest as beings — the ground of poverty-in-world (§58, p.236 / pdf 130).
ontologyNodes.text: Heidegger - The Fundamental Concepts of Metaphysics

ontologyNodes.name: Disinhibiting ring
ontologyNodes.definition: The encircling ring of disinhibitors within which animal behaviour is driven; Heidegger's recasting of Uexküll's Umwelt (§60b, p.253 / pdf 139; §61b, p.261 / pdf 143).
ontologyNodes.text: Heidegger - The Fundamental Concepts of Metaphysics

ontologyNodes.name: The 'as'-structure
ontologyNodes.definition: The taking of beings as beings, read from the apophantic logos; the structural core of world-formation that the animal lacks (§69, p.287 / pdf 156; §72, p.304 / pdf 164).
ontologyNodes.text: Heidegger - The Fundamental Concepts of Metaphysics

ontologyNodes.name: Projection
ontologyNodes.definition: The primordial structure of the tripartite occurrence of world-formation; the prevailing of world that lets beings as a whole prevail (§76, p.360 / pdf 192).
ontologyNodes.text: Heidegger - The Fundamental Concepts of Metaphysics

ontologyNodes.name: World as accessibility of beings
ontologyNodes.translation: world as the accessibility/manifestness of beings as beings
ontologyNodes.definition: The provisional and then settled definition of world reached comparatively in Part Two (§47, p.196 / pdf 110; §68, p.282 / pdf 153).
ontologyNodes.text: Heidegger - The Fundamental Concepts of Metaphysics

ontologyNodes.name: Being-there / being-away
ontologyNodes.definition: The polarity on whose ground the being-there and not-being-there of attunement is grasped, displacing the consciousness/unconsciousness distinction (§16c, p.63 / pdf 44).
ontologyNodes.text: Heidegger - The Fundamental Concepts of Metaphysics

ontologyNodes.name: Homesickness
ontologyNodes.definition: Novalis's name (taken up by Heidegger) for the fundamental attunement of philosophizing — an urge to be at home everywhere (§2, p.5 / pdf 14).
ontologyNodes.text: Heidegger - The Fundamental Concepts of Metaphysics

ontologyNodes.name: physis
ontologyNodes.definition: The self-forming prevailing of beings as a whole; with two meanings distinguished in Aristotle (§8, p.25 / pdf 24; §9, p.32 / pdf 28).
ontologyNodes.text: Heidegger - The Fundamental Concepts of Metaphysics

ontologyNodes.name: alētheia
ontologyNodes.definition: Truth as something torn from concealment; the unconcealed that logos exhibits (§8, p.27 / pdf 25).
ontologyNodes.text: Heidegger - The Fundamental Concepts of Metaphysics

ontologyNodes.name: apophantic logos
ontologyNodes.definition: The assertion that lets beings be seen as what and how they are; the locus from which the "as"-structure of world-formation is read (Aristotle, De Interpretatione; §72, p.304 / pdf 164).
ontologyNodes.text: Heidegger - The Fundamental Concepts of Metaphysics

ontologyNodes.name: Ambience / Ambient
ontologyNodes.definition: The ontological condition in which the surrounding environment is not a passive container or backdrop but an active, generative, immersive ground from which things, meanings, and rhetorical situations emerge. Ambience is less driven by connection (as in networks) and more resonant with immersion, permeation, and osmosis. It names the dynamic, emergent ecology of coadapting elements -- human, nonhuman, material, technological, environmental -- that compose the world prior to and exceeding any subject-object division.

ontologyNodes.name: Ambient Rhetoric
ontologyNodes.definition: Rhetoric reconceived as the always-ongoing disclosure of the world that shifts our manner of being in that world, rather than a discrete symbolic act performed by autonomous human agents upon passive audiences. Ambient rhetoric encompasses material things, nonhuman agencies, ecological assemblages, attunement, and the withdrawal of objects from relation. It is "disclosure itself becoming affective, suasive" (Conclusion, 281) and is fundamentally preparatory rather than paradigmatic.

ontologyNodes.name: Attunement / Stimmung
ontologyNodes.definition: Heidegger's ontological concept of mood (*Stimmung*) reconceived as the fundamental disclosure of the world that precedes cognition, volition, and intention. Attunement is not a subjective state of mind or willed comportment but "an ambient catalysis within what is most material and concrete, a gathering that springs forward" (Ch2, 98). It is "like an atmosphere in which we first immerse ourselves in each case and which then attunes us through and through" (*FCM* 67). Attunement grounds ambient rhetoric as the condition under which things, situations, and persuasive forces show up at all.

ontologyNodes.name: Disclosure / Aletheia
ontologyNodes.definition: The Heideggerian concept of truth as unconcealment: things come to presence in a particular way, always also concealing other aspects. Disclosure is always ongoing, never exhaustive, and never solely the doing of human beings. In Rickert's culminating formulation, "rhetoric is ambience as affective disclosure" (Conclusion, 281). Every act of unconcealing is simultaneously a concealing, which means rhetoric must attend to what withdraws as well as what appears.

ontologyNodes.name: Dwelling
ontologyNodes.definition: Not mere habitation but an ontological, ecological relationship between humans, things, and environments. Dwelling is "activity conditioned by the land and the things of the world" (Ch7, 243) -- the ongoing process of building, disclosure, and attunement through which humans and nonhumans coexist. "Dwelling built the farmhouse, not the peasants per se" (Ch7, 243). Dwelling is the mode through which affectability becomes rhetoric conceived ambiently, and it is inherently ethical insofar as it gives rise to values through practice rather than human projection.

ontologyNodes.name: Ecology
ontologyNodes.definition: The relational, mutually constitutive field of human and nonhuman elements, opposed to "environment" understood as a passive container. Derived from Greek *oikos* (household/dwelling place), ecology names the condition in which things, organisms, materials, and practices condition and support one another. Rhetoric is ecological insofar as its action is "material, affective, ecological, and emergent" (Ch3, 129).

ontologyNodes.name: Fourfold
ontologyNodes.definition: Heidegger's gathering of earth, sky, divinities, and mortals in things. Not four separate categories but a "onefold" in which each element mirrors and rings in the others, constituting an ongoing interplay of presence and withdrawal. The fourfold is lived first and philosophized second; it is the framework through which dwelling takes its bearings. Things "gather" the fourfold, as in the jug example where wine, water, spring, earth, and sky are all gathered in the poured gift.

ontologyNodes.name: Rhetorical Being
ontologyNodes.definition: The condition of being-in-the-world as inherently rhetorical -- not a rhetorical agent who deploys persuasive techniques but a being whose very existence is constituted by the ambient disclosure of world. Rhetoric is not something one does but something one is immersed in. Rhetorical being names "the synthesis of multiple content threads of varying intensities" (Ch4, 133) gathered within material and affective environments.

ontologyNodes.name: Thing / Gathering
ontologyNodes.definition: A thing is not a mere object but a gathering of concerns, relations, and situations. Etymologically, Old English *thing*/*ting* = assembly for deliberation; Latin *res* = matter of discourse; the Icelandic *Althing* = parliament. Things gather the fourfold and participate in rhetoric as material agents of disclosure. The "rhetorical thing" (Ch6) names material participants in the ambient disclosure of world -- not merely objects of persuasion but co-constituents of rhetorical situations.

ontologyNodes.name: Chora
ontologyNodes.definition: The Platonic "third kind" (*triton genos*) from the *Timaeus* -- neither Form nor material copy but a generative, withdrawing matrix or receptacle from which all becoming, beginning, and creation emerge. Rickert recovers *chora* through Kristeva (semiotic/affective), Derrida (deconstructive/aporetic), and Ulmer (inventional/performative) to show that rhetoric and invention rest on an "infomaterial" ground that reveals and conceals simultaneously. The *chora* is the ancient precursor to ambience: "Place is not simply an immediate environment; it includes the background by means of which things show up" (Ch1, 55).

ontologyNodes.name: Nonhuman Agency
ontologyNodes.definition: Agency distributed across human and nonhuman actants -- not a projection of human agency onto objects but an acknowledgment of their performative operationality emergent from material, contextual, and relational conditions. Theorized through Latour's actant concept, Harman's tool-being, Bennett's vital materialism, and Brooks's subsumption architecture. Material things exercise persuasion irreducible to symbolic mediation (speed bumps, Berlin Key, electrical grid).

ontologyNodes.name: Embodiment / Embodied Cognition
ontologyNodes.definition: The condition of being bodily situated in and constituted by a material environment. Drawing on Clark's extended cognition, Dourish's embodied interaction, and Heidegger's being-in-the-world, Rickert argues that minds are "at once embodied and dispersed into the environment" -- composites of intellect, body, information, and material scaffoldings. Embodiment grounds the ambient claim that rhetoric is material, not merely symbolic.

ontologyNodes.name: Invention
ontologyNodes.definition: Rhetorical invention reconceived as fundamentally emplaced -- arising not from autonomous rational method but from the generative matrix of material, affective, and environmental relations. Invention is something that happens *through* the coinvention of subject, place, and circumstance. Kristeva's *chora* shows invention exceeds the range of symbolicity; Ulmer's chorography practically enacts choric invention; Verbal Kint demonstrates "inventive passivity before the ambient environs."

ontologyNodes.name: Worldliness / Being-in-the-World
ontologyNodes.definition: Heidegger's foundational claim that Dasein is always already thrown into a world of practical involvements -- not a subject confronting objects but a being immersed in meaningful situations. From this ground, language, rhetoric, and invention emerge. Worldliness means that the world is simultaneously material and meaningful, never exhausted by the presence of material things, and rhetoric is "a response to the way the world attunes and speaks us" (Ch5, 189).

ontologyNodes.name: Withdrawal
ontologyNodes.definition: The ontological condition whereby objects, meanings, and the world itself are never fully present to any relation. Things always reserve depths that exceed human knowledge, use, and attribution. Withdrawal is not absence but "a form of supporting" (Ch7, 244) -- the condition of possibility for ongoing disclosure. It ensures that the world is always more than what we make of it. Theorized through Harman's tool-being, Heidegger's concealment, and the *chora*'s generative recession.

ontologyNodes.name: Networks
ontologyNodes.definition: Treated as ontological rather than merely technological -- "a principle of being" in which subjects emerge as nodular points within coadaptive threads (via Taylor's complexity theory). However, Rickert argues the network metaphor is necessary but insufficient for ambient rhetoric because it remains invested in binaries (node/link, foreground/background) and lacks the immersive, osmotic, material thickness that ambience requires. Ambience supplements and exceeds the network.

ontologyNodes.name: Periechon
ontologyNodes.definition: Greek term meaning "that which surrounds, encompasses, or makes room for." Appears alongside *chora* in Plato's *Timaeus* and connects to the sense of a surrounding cosmos that is itself alive. Rickert identifies it as the ancient Greek precursor to the concept of ambience and returns to it in the book's final sentence as what ambient rhetoric recovers: "a renewed sensibility to what the ancient Greeks called *periechon*" (Conclusion, 285).

ontologyNodes.name: Technics / Technology
ontologyNodes.definition: Technology understood not merely as instrumental tool but as disclosive -- it reveals how we are in the world (connecting to Heidegger's *Question Concerning Technology*). Rickert maintains a dual stance: technology makes ambient conditions newly visible (Eno, ambientROOM, EV1), yet technological solutions to technologically produced problems risk entrenching us deeper in technological thinking (enframing). The *chora* dissolves the *techne*/*physis* distinction.

ontologyNodes.name: Terroir
ontologyNodes.definition: The irreducible somewhereness of wine rooted in earth, climate, practice, and place. Serves as the book's governing figure from the Preface onward, returned to in the Conclusion as a "material-social-hermeneutic ecology." Terroir grounds the claim that rhetoric, like winemaking, is constituted by material relations that exceed human intention and control.

ontologyNodes.name: Sufficiency
ontologyNodes.definition: Not a countervalue to be adopted but an ontological attunement materialized through dwelling practices. Opposed to the ambient logic of efficiency that pervades modern life. Sufficiency "emerges as a principle only insofar as we can abstract it from already ongoing dwelling" (Ch8, 257). Demonstrated through Toronto Island's resistance to automobility.

ontologyNodes.name: Electracy
ontologyNodes.definition: Ulmer's term for the emerging cultural epoch shaped by electronic media, analogous to literacy's relation to print. Electracy is itself choric -- "a third kind, following but being neither progress from nor a hybrid of orality and literacy" (Ch1, 68). New media and ambient intelligence make choric invention's emplaced, distributed character newly visible.

ontologyNodes.name: Soundmarks
ontologyNodes.definition: R. Murray Schafer's term for the sonic counterpart to landmarks -- culturally valued sounds that define and organize communities. Distinguished from keynotes (ambient background sounds) and signals (meaningful foreground sounds). Used in Ch4 to demonstrate that sound is woven into the fabric of dwelling and rhetoric, not ornamental addition.

ontologyNodes.name: Assemblage
ontologyNodes.definition: Bennett's term (via Deleuze): a historical, contingent grouping of disparate actants generating power along a continuum, vitally inserted into larger assemblages that exceed and conflict with constituent actants. The university, the electrical grid, Toronto Island are all assemblages. Extends Latour's actant concept by emphasizing nested complexity and uneven power distribution.

ontologyNodes.name: Preparatory Rhetoric
ontologyNodes.definition: Rhetoric conceived not as direct persuasion but as groundwork that lays conditions for disclosure and transformed dwelling. The book itself is "ultimately only preparatory" (Ch8, 269). Ambient rhetoric "cannot short-circuit itself into being a new paradigm" but can only attune, lay groundwork, and open conditions of possibility.

ontologyNodes.name: Umwelt
ontologyNodes.definition: Closed perceptual-active world of a subject, composed of Merkwelt + Wirkwelt; each organism inhabits its own Umwelt, which contains only subjective realities. Reframed in Part II as a voice in Nature's world-score, constituted by meaning-relations.
ontologyNodes.text: Von Uexkull - A Foray into the Worlds of Animals and Humans

ontologyNodes.name: Funktionskreis (functional cycle)
ontologyNodes.definition: Closed loop linking subject and object via perception organ and effect organ; the basic unit of organism-environment interaction. Perception mark activates the cycle; effect mark extinguishes the perception mark, closing it. Reframed as Bedeutungskreis (meaning cycle) in Part II.
ontologyNodes.text: Von Uexkull - A Foray into the Worlds of Animals and Humans

ontologyNodes.name: Merkwelt (perception world)
ontologyNodes.definition: Totality of what the subject perceives; the perceptual half of the Umwelt.
ontologyNodes.text: Von Uexkull - A Foray into the Worlds of Animals and Humans

ontologyNodes.name: Wirkwelt (effect world)
ontologyNodes.definition: Totality of what the subject can affect through action; the active half of the Umwelt.
ontologyNodes.text: Von Uexkull - A Foray into the Worlds of Animals and Humans

ontologyNodes.name: Merkmal (perception mark)
ontologyNodes.definition: Quality of an object as it appears in a subject's Umwelt; external mark "read off" the object by the subject's perception apparatus. Distinguished from the internal Merkzeichen.
ontologyNodes.text: Von Uexkull - A Foray into the Worlds of Animals and Humans

ontologyNodes.name: Wirkmal (effect mark)
ontologyNodes.definition: Mark imprinted on the object by the subject's effector; cancels the perception mark, closing the functional cycle.
ontologyNodes.text: Von Uexkull - A Foray into the Worlds of Animals and Humans

ontologyNodes.name: Merkzeichen (perception sign)
ontologyNodes.definition: Internal sign generated by perception cells; transposed outward it becomes a perception mark on the object. Recast as Merkton (perception tone) in Part II's musical framework.
ontologyNodes.text: Von Uexkull - A Foray into the Worlds of Animals and Humans

ontologyNodes.name: Gegengefuge (counterstructure)
ontologyNodes.definition: Structural link within the object between perception-mark carrier and effect-mark carrier; the object-side nexus of the functional cycle. Replaced by Komplement (complement) in Part II's subject-side analysis.
ontologyNodes.text: Von Uexkull - A Foray into the Worlds of Animals and Humans

ontologyNodes.name: Bedeutung (meaning)
ontologyNodes.definition: Functional significance an object holds for an organism; evolves from relational property ("the only certain guide," U-F3) to universal ontological bond ("meaning ruled them all," U-M6).
ontologyNodes.text: Von Uexkull - A Foray into the Worlds of Animals and Humans

ontologyNodes.name: Bedeutungstrager (carrier of meaning)
ontologyNodes.definition: Object transformed by entering a meaning-relation with a subject; bears meaning conferred by that subject. Replaces "object" as the fundamental category in Part II.
ontologyNodes.text: Von Uexkull - A Foray into the Worlds of Animals and Humans

ontologyNodes.name: Bauplan (construction plan)
ontologyNodes.definition: Structural plan governing the composition of either an organism's body or its environment; species-specific. Extended in Part II to environmental construction plans and subordinated to the Bedeutungsregel (meaning rule).
ontologyNodes.text: Von Uexkull - A Foray into the Worlds of Animals and Humans

ontologyNodes.name: Planmassigkeit (conformity to plan)
ontologyNodes.definition: Nature's structural design governing organism-environment fit; replaces teleological goal-attribution with non-intentional purposiveness. Oscillates between heuristic and metaphysical readings.
ontologyNodes.text: Von Uexkull - A Foray into the Worlds of Animals and Humans

ontologyNodes.name: Kompositionslehre (composition theory)
ontologyNodes.definition: The general theory of how Nature composes organisms and their environments contrapuntally; the capstone framework of the Theory of Meaning.
ontologyNodes.text: Von Uexkull - A Foray into the Worlds of Animals and Humans

ontologyNodes.name: Kontrapunkt (counterpoint)
ontologyNodes.definition: Point-for-point structural-functional correspondence between organism properties and environmental properties. "Were the flower not bee-like, the consonance could never work."
ontologyNodes.text: Von Uexkull - A Foray into the Worlds of Animals and Humans

ontologyNodes.name: Wohnhulle (dwelling-shell)
ontologyNodes.definition: The plant's equivalent of an animal's Umwelt; composed of meaning factors (wind, rain, sunlight) rather than carriers of meaning processed through functional cycles.
ontologyNodes.text: Von Uexkull - A Foray into the Worlds of Animals and Humans

ontologyNodes.name: Subjekt (subject)
ontologyNodes.definition: Organism as perceiver and agent; constitutes its own Umwelt. "Without a living subject, there can be neither space nor time." In Part II, becomes both meaning-utilizer and meaning-recipient.
ontologyNodes.text: Von Uexkull - A Foray into the Worlds of Animals and Humans

ontologyNodes.name: Ton / Tonung (tone)
ontologyNodes.definition: Functional coloring an object acquires in a given Umwelt (sitting tone, danger tone, feeding tone, etc.). Expands from perceptual affordance (Part I) to meaning-tone as compositional element in the world-score (Part II).
ontologyNodes.text: Von Uexkull - A Foray into the Worlds of Animals and Humans

ontologyNodes.name: Eigenton / Ich-Ton (self-tone)
ontologyNodes.definition: Intrinsic qualitative response of a living cell to any stimulus; fundamental unit of biosemiotic responsiveness. Builds upward: cell tone -> organ tone -> life tone -> organism symphony.
ontologyNodes.text: Von Uexkull - A Foray into the Worlds of Animals and Humans

ontologyNodes.name: Urbild (primal image)
ontologyNodes.definition: Non-physical archetype guiding morphogenesis and cross-species meaning relations; the spider's web conforms to the Urbild of the fly, not any particular fly. Carries Goethean and Aristotelian (eidos) resonance.
ontologyNodes.text: Von Uexkull - A Foray into the Worlds of Animals and Humans

ontologyNodes.name: Bedeutungsregel (meaning rule)
ontologyNodes.definition: General directive that assigns a functional role independent of species-specific form; bridges carrier and utilizer of meaning. Distinguished from Bauplanregel (form development rule).
ontologyNodes.text: Von Uexkull - A Foray into the Worlds of Animals and Humans

ontologyNodes.name: Bildungsmelodie (formative melody)
ontologyNodes.definition: Immaterial organizational principle directing morphogenesis from germ cell; plays on the "clavier" of genes. Declared inscrutable but real.
ontologyNodes.text: Von Uexkull - A Foray into the Worlds of Animals and Humans

ontologyNodes.name: Stimmung (mood)
ontologyNodes.definition: Internal state of the subject that determines which effect image (and hence which meaning-tone) is activated for a given perception image. Structural parallel to Heidegger's Befindlichkeit.
ontologyNodes.text: Von Uexkull - A Foray into the Worlds of Animals and Humans

ontologyNodes.name: Merkbild / Wahrnehmungsbild (perception image)
ontologyNodes.definition: Composite sensory representation of an object; higher-order than individual perception marks. Requires organized schemata (open/closed) in perception cells. Bees possess genuine Merkbilder; lower organisms do not.
ontologyNodes.text: Von Uexkull - A Foray into the Worlds of Animals and Humans

ontologyNodes.name: Wirkbild (effect image)
ontologyNodes.definition: Representation of the act the subject performs upon an object; completes and alters the perception image, conferring meaning. Mood determines which effect image activates.
ontologyNodes.text: Von Uexkull - A Foray into the Worlds of Animals and Humans

ontologyNodes.name: Suchbild / Suchton (search image / search tone)
ontologyNodes.definition: Internally generated perceptual template (search image) or functional orientation (search tone) guiding searching; can override actual perception images. A "free production of the subject."
ontologyNodes.text: Von Uexkull - A Foray into the Worlds of Animals and Humans

ontologyNodes.name: Moment / Merkzeit (moment / perception time)
ontologyNodes.definition: Species-specific smallest indivisible unit of experienced time (human = 1/18th sec); determines the temporal grain of the Umwelt.
ontologyNodes.text: Von Uexkull - A Foray into the Worlds of Animals and Humans

ontologyNodes.name: Wirkraum / Tastraum / Sehraum
ontologyNodes.definition: Three interpenetrating subject-constituted spaces: effect space (directional steps), tactile space (places via local signs), visual space (visual elements bounded by farthest plane). No universal shared space.
ontologyNodes.text: Von Uexkull - A Foray into the Worlds of Animals and Humans

ontologyNodes.name: Umgebung (surroundings)
ontologyNodes.definition: Objective surroundings; what remains when the Umwelt is stripped. The substrate all Umwelten excerpt. Nature-in-itself "carries and shelters all environments" but is never fully known.
ontologyNodes.text: Von Uexkull - A Foray into the Worlds of Animals and Humans

ontologyNodes.name: Bedeutungsverwertung (meaning utilization)
ontologyNodes.definition: Process by which organisms utilize carriers of meaning according to their structural plan; functional cycles reframed as meaning cycles.
ontologyNodes.text: Von Uexkull - A Foray into the Worlds of Animals and Humans

ontologyNodes.name: Bedeutungsduldung (sufferance of meaning)
ontologyNodes.definition: Passive reception of meaning against the interest of the receiving subject (fly in web, plant being grazed). Graded from harmless to ruinous; serves species-level equilibrium.
ontologyNodes.text: Von Uexkull - A Foray into the Worlds of Animals and Humans

ontologyNodes.name: Naturpartitur (score of Nature)
ontologyNodes.definition: Comprehensive contrapuntal description of meaning-relations among all organisms in a habitat; biology's task is to "write the score of Nature."
ontologyNodes.text: Von Uexkull - A Foray into the Worlds of Animals and Humans

ontologyNodes.name: Bedeutungskeim (meaning-germ)
ontologyNodes.definition: Originary meaning-nucleus from which an organism crystallizes; the acorn is the meaning-germ of the oak. Final concept of the book.
ontologyNodes.text: Von Uexkull - A Foray into the Worlds of Animals and Humans

ontologyNodes.name: Magische Umwelt (magical environment)
ontologyNodes.definition: Environment containing phenomena visible only to the subject, arising without external stimuli; includes search images, inborn paths, and innate behavioral sequences.
ontologyNodes.text: Von Uexkull - A Foray into the Worlds of Animals and Humans

ontologyNodes.name: Reflexrepublik (reflex republic)
ontologyNodes.definition: Organism (sea urchin) composed of autonomous reflex persons coordinating without central direction. Contrasted with centrally directed organisms and the tick's integrated perception.
ontologyNodes.text: Von Uexkull - A Foray into the Worlds of Animals and Humans

ontologyNodes.name: Wirkzeichen (effect sign)
ontologyNodes.definition: Internal sign generated by effect cells; triggers motor impulses that produce effect marks. Counterpart to Merkzeichen.
ontologyNodes.text: Von Uexkull - A Foray into the Worlds of Animals and Humans

ontologyNodes.name: Dramatism (method-name)
ontologyNodes.definition: Burke's titular method-name: motives analyzed in a perspective developed from the analysis of drama, treating language and thought primarily as modes of action rather than modes of representation. The Grammar is the foundational volume of a projected dramatistic trilogy (Grammar / Rhetoric / Symbolic).

ontologyNodes.name: The pentad (five key terms of dramatism)
ontologyNodes.definition: Act / Scene / Agent / Agency / Purpose — the five irreducible terms of motive-statement, offered as the generating principle of dramatistic analysis. Each term answers a single interrogative (what / where-or-when / who / how / why). The pentad is a system of placement rather than a historical survey; transcendental rather than formal (Kantian in scope).

ontologyNodes.name: Act (pentad term)
ontologyNodes.definition: The pentad term answering 'what was done?' On the scholastic-realist construal Burke develops in GM-06, an act is an actualization (energeia) — the bringing of a potentiality into realization in accordance with a form proper to its kind. Distinguishable from mere motion (which lies in the realm of instruments); admits a spectrum (attitude, incipient act, delayed act) and is reciprocally related to potency. Featured by Realism (Aristotle/Aquinas).

ontologyNodes.name: Scene (pentad term)
ontologyNodes.definition: The pentad term answering 'where/in what situation?' Names the background, setting, situation, or containing environment within which an act occurs and an agent moves. As containing-principle for action, scene fixes the circumference within which motive may be located. Featured by Materialism (Hobbes, Spinoza, Darwin, Lucretius, Stoicism). Spinoza's universal substance is the maximal-circumference instance.

ontologyNodes.name: Agent (pentad term)
ontologyNodes.definition: The pentad term answering 'who did it?' Names the constituting subject — the doer of the act, from which (on idealist construal) scene, act, agency, and purpose are derived. Admits subdivision into co-agents and counter-agents and generalization into super-agents (church, race, nation, Spirit, class). Featured by Idealism (Berkeley, Hume, Leibniz, Kant, Hegel) — and by Marxism as a hybrid 'idealistic materialist' (class-as-collective-agent under materialist surface).

ontologyNodes.name: Agency (pentad term)
ontologyNodes.definition: The pentad term answering 'how? by what means?' Names the instruments, methods, and mediating media through which an act is performed. Paradigmatic in tools, machines, and the pragmatist nesting of file/hand/brain/educational-system. Featured by Pragmatism (James, Dewey, Mead, Peirce, Bridgman) — the modern, science-driven inversion of Aristotle's subordination of agency under final cause: 'means become ancestors of ends.'

ontologyNodes.name: Purpose (pentad term)
ontologyNodes.definition: The pentad term answering 'why?' Names the end, telos, motivating-toward-which of an act. The term most subject to violent disagreement among motive-attributors. Featured by Mysticism (Plotinus, Plato's Good=One, Bonaventura, Christian mystics) — recognizable not by mere unity but by 'unity of the individual with some cosmic or universal Purpose.' Most susceptible to dissolution: pure Purpose collapses into the paradox of substance (docta ignorantia) and survives implicitly even where formally eliminated.

ontologyNodes.name: Scene-act ratio
ontologyNodes.definition: The dyadic ratio whereby the quality of the scene implies (contains, calls forth) a correspondingly qualified act, and convertibly the act demands or constructs a scene of corresponding quality. Reversible; usable deterministically or hortatorily. The chapter-titular ratio of GM-01 'Container and Thing Contained' and the prediction-engine of dramatistic analysis (Burke's deployment in the Keats Ode worked example, GM-10).

ontologyNodes.name: Scene-agent ratio
ontologyNodes.definition: The dyadic ratio whereby person and place stand in synecdochic correspondence: the quality of a place implies a corresponding quality of inhabitant; the contents of a divine container share in its divinity. Positional in the strong sense (scene contains agent). Worked at length in nineteenth-century idealist 'Einklang zwischen Innen- und Aussenwelt' and in the naturalist-novelist embarrassment (brutalizing scene yields brutal characters).

ontologyNodes.name: Scene-agency ratio
ontologyNodes.definition: The dyadic ratio between scene and the instrumental means employed in an act. The scene affords/constrains which agencies are available; conversely, new agencies (technologies, methods) accumulate to become scenic — Burke's Biddle example: railroad, telegraph, telephone, automobile, radio 'having in their accumulation become scenic' motivate political acts.

ontologyNodes.name: Scene-purpose ratio
ontologyNodes.definition: The dyadic ratio between scene and the purpose toward which an act tends. A scene affords particular purpose-structures (quest-givers, eschatological horizons, providential cosmos); conversely a purpose may project a scene proportioned to it. Hegelian Reason-as-Grundprinzip is its paradigm idealist deployment; the Stoic cosmic-providential plan is its materialist (pronoia) deployment.

ontologyNodes.name: Act-agent ratio
ontologyNodes.definition: The dyadic ratio between an act and the agent who performs it. NOT a strict containment relation: 'the agent does not contain the act, though its results might be said to pre-exist virtually within him.' Temporal/sequential: agents author acts; acts can in turn make or remake the agent. Burke's signature examples: 'sobering influence of the Presidency,' judicial robes, Russian wartime resistance (act-agent vs scene-act as competing readings). Scholastic-realist primary ratio: 'every thing acts according as it is in act' (Aquinas).

ontologyNodes.name: Act-agency ratio
ontologyNodes.definition: The dyadic ratio between act and the instrumental means employed to perform it. Burke's way-words discussion (hodos / tao / yoga / dike → met-hodos as method-as-means) is the chapter's clearest formulation of the act/agency boundary instability: an act-word (way of life) becomes an agency-word (means of doing) by a subtle slide from being to doing.

ontologyNodes.name: Act-purpose ratio
ontologyNodes.definition: The dyadic ratio between act and the purpose toward which it tends. An act is consummated only insofar as it realizes the purpose for the sake of which it is done; conversely a purpose is articulate only insofar as it admits expression in a concrete act. The Aeschylean Erinyes→Eumenides transformation is Burke's paradigm of act-purpose total transformation.

ontologyNodes.name: Agent-agency ratio
ontologyNodes.definition: The dyadic ratio between an agent and the instrumental means available to (or characteristic of) that agent. Agent-character implies a corresponding set of fit agencies; conversely, habituated agencies constitute the agent's character. The Seurat-pointillism case (book p. 8) is a borderline instance where the medium becomes the common element relating agent to scene.

ontologyNodes.name: Agent-purpose ratio
ontologyNodes.definition: The dyadic ratio between an agent and the purpose toward which the agent's action tends. Burke locates 'needs' as 'a property of agents,' making agent-purpose the relation between an agent's needs/wants/aspirations and the purposes they generate. Distinguishes 'primal needs' (proper to agent) from 'new needs' (which may best be treated as scenic).

ontologyNodes.name: Agency-purpose ratio
ontologyNodes.definition: The dyadic ratio between the instrumental means and the purpose for which they are employed. Agency tends to acquire its own teleology under sustained use ('philosophy of means'); purpose conversely shapes which agencies are admissible. The chapter-titular ratio of GM-07; the dialectical hinge between Pragmatism (Agency-feature) and Mysticism (Purpose-feature). Burke's 'Mysticism of Means' critique (Huxley pacifism) is its most worked instance.

ontologyNodes.name: Reversibility of ratios (10 → 20)
ontologyNodes.definition: Burke's principle (GM-01, GM-06) that each ratio operates in both directions: scene-act reads either as scene-implies-act or as act-demands-scene; the ten dyadic ratios expand to twenty reversible ratios. 'A ratio is a formula indicating a transition from one term to another'; the mediated necessarily differs from the immediate, as translation differs from original. The 1962 Addendum (GM-09) sharpens: order of terms matters (scene-act ≠ act-scene).

ontologyNodes.name: Ratios as principles of determination / selectivity
ontologyNodes.definition: Burke's strong formulation: the ratios are 'principles of determination' — the analytical engine of dramatism, not merely a catalogue. Softened reading: principles of selectivity (a situation 'votes for' appropriate temperaments and acts rather than producing them ex nihilo; 'mute inglorious Miltons' as unselected seeds). The choice between competing ratios is rhetorically consequential — ratio-selection deflects attention from one motive-locus to another.

ontologyNodes.name: Metaphor / perspective (master trope)
ontologyNodes.definition: The device for seeing something in terms of something else — bringing out the thisness of a that. Literal-realistic substitution: perspective. To consider A from the point of view of B is to use B as a perspective on A. Reality is not dissolved by multi-perspectivism; it is established by it. Degrees of being correspond to variety-of-perspectives-supportable (plants > minerals; animals > plants; men > animals).

ontologyNodes.name: Metonymy / reduction (master trope)
ontologyNodes.definition: Conveying an incorporeal or intangible state in terms of the corporeal or tangible ('heart' for 'emotions'); the 'archaicizing' device. Reduction is the one-direction (quality-to-quantity) special case proper to scientific realism. Two senses: poet's metonymy as figure/symbolization vs. scientific behaviorist's metonymy as substantial reduction. The trope underwrites materialism's scene-featuring.

ontologyNodes.name: Synecdoche / representation (master trope)
ontologyNodes.definition: Convertibility between two terms in an integral relationship: part for whole, whole for part, container for contained, sign for signified, cause for effect, genus for species, and all reversals. The 'noblest synecdoche' is microcosm-macrocosm identity (Leibniz). Two-way (unlike metonymy's one-way). Burke extends to before/after, implicit/explicit, name/narrative, disease/cure, hero/villain, active/passive. Underwrites every representative-anecdote choice.

ontologyNodes.name: Irony / dialectic (master trope)
ontologyNodes.definition: Arises when one tries, by the interaction of terms upon one another, to produce a development that uses all the terms. From the standpoint of this total form ('perspective of perspectives'), no participating sub-perspective is precisely right or precisely wrong; all are voices integrally affecting one another. True/classic/humble irony is grounded in consubstantiality with the 'enemy' (Flaubert, Mann, Newton, Falstaff); romantic/Pharisaic irony is grounded in superiority. The over-all formula: A → non-A (the peripety).

ontologyNodes.name: Paradox of substance
ontologyNodes.definition: The structural irony at the root of all substance-talk: the word designates what a thing intrinsically is, but etymologically refers to something outside the thing that stands beneath or supports it (sub-stance, hypostasis, stā- root). Every substance-claim covertly imports a contextual reference into an intrinsic claim. The master-irony of GM-02 from which the substance-vocabulary taxonomy is derived; recapitulated as a dialectical staple in GM-09.

ontologyNodes.name: Contextual / geometric substance
ontologyNodes.definition: Definition by placement of a thing within its context, location, or surroundings. To define (de-finire) is to mark boundaries, requiring reference to what is outside the thing. Maximalist version: Spinoza's universal substance, where each object is determined by the totality (omnis determinatio est negatio). Geometric subspecies: Euclidean-Spinozistic implicit-relation calculus.

ontologyNodes.name: Familial (tribal, ancestral) substance
ontologyNodes.definition: Defining a substance by ancestral cause — biological descent or spiritualized analogue (covenant, founder, eponym, creation). Includes Plato's archetypal Forms (each thing imitating its eponym in heaven) and Aristotle's entelechy (the individual as actualization of its class). Mediaeval universalia debate (ante rem / in re / post rem) is its scholastic refraction.

ontologyNodes.name: Directional substance
ontologyNodes.definition: Substance characterized by motion toward, by 'the way,' by direction-from-within. Strongly futuristic and purposive ('Where are you going?' rather than 'Where are you from?'). Includes the cluster motion / movement / cause / emotion / moment as variant glosses on motivation.

ontologyNodes.name: Dialectic substance
ontologyNodes.definition: The over-all substance category: substance arising from the systematic contemplation of antinomies — recognition that we necessarily define a thing in terms of something else, where the something else is the other (the antagonist, the agon). The dramatistic super-category that subsumes contextual / familial / directional / geometric substance-types.

ontologyNodes.name: Paradox of purity (pure substance flips to its negation)
ontologyNodes.greek: pure substance flips to its negation
ontologyNodes.definition: When a substance is purified by abstraction to its absolute, it tends toward its negation: God as 'pure person' is impersonal; pure being is not-being (Hegel); pure escape is perpetual imprisonment in escape; Aristotle's God as Pure Act = eternal repose. Plotinus's negative theology arrives at abstract Oneness by negating all material attributes.

ontologyNodes.name: Actus / status (action-state dyad)
ontologyNodes.definition: Burke's load-bearing dyadic reduction of the tragic triad (poiema/pathema/mathema): act vs. state, motion vs. rest, drama vs. lyric, faith-as-act vs. knowledge-as-state. Maps onto potentiality/actuality and tracks the philological drift by which active terms (aretē, virtus, hero) become state-terms ('L'état c'est moi'). Articulates the substance vocabulary with the Act-Agent ratio of the pentad.

ontologyNodes.name: Intrinsic / extrinsic substance
ontologyNodes.definition: The dialectical pairing of motivations-within-the-agent against motivations-derived-from-scene. Hegel pairs Matter (extrinsic, gravity-externally-referred) with Spirit (intrinsic, Bei-sich-selbst-sein). The poles invert structurally when an intrinsic principle is operationalized through external means. The intrinsic must not be confused with the unique. GM-11 generalizes this as the scope-of-text question and resolves it via the poem-as-act framework.

ontologyNodes.name: Rhetorical substance
ontologyNodes.definition: The ambiguity of substance as a deployable resource of persuasion. 'Substantially,' 'essentially,' 'in principle,' 'in the long run' allow a speaker to assert identity at a level of generality that cannot be falsified by particulars. Positivists who outlaw substance reimport it covertly under 'in-principle' and 'universally valid.'

ontologyNodes.name: Consubstantial substance (epithetic, identificatory)
ontologyNodes.definition: Substance as it operates in epithets and identification-tactics: to call a man brother is to proclaim consubstantiality; to call him bastard is to attack his familial 'authorship.' An epithet assigns substance doubly — characterizes the object and implies an action toward it, thus serving as motive. Forward-anchors the consubstantiation/identification apparatus of A Rhetoric of Motives (1950).

ontologyNodes.name: Universal motive / monetary substance (money as god-term)
ontologyNodes.definition: When a substance becomes a universal motive, it operates as a master scene supplying believers with a common motivational ground. Monotheism and the monetary motive are structurally parallel; money 'transubstantiates' from agency (medium of exchange) into ground/purpose of action — the 'capitalist psychosis.' GM-08 develops money as God-term of constitutional frames ('where one can volunteer, there one is free').

ontologyNodes.name: Representative anecdote
ontologyNodes.definition: The compact case that condenses the analytical pattern Burke will then expand into a full terminology; the form 'in conformity with which the vocabulary is constructed.' A good representative anecdote is to a vocabulary of motives what a paradigm is to a research program — its scope-limiter and its generative seed. Drama is Burke's representative anecdote for human motives; behaviorist conditioned reflex is the negative example. GM-13 contrasts representative vs. reductive anecdote.

ontologyNodes.name: Circumference (scope of scene)
ontologyNodes.definition: The analyst's elected scope-of-scene; the size of the contextual frame within which an act is located. Burke's most transferable methodological construct after the pentad itself. Selection of circumference 'is in itself an act, an act of faith.' Different circumferences yield different motives for the same act. The historical narrowing-of-circumference (God's law → natural law → environment → monetary scene) is Burke's structural account of secularization.

ontologyNodes.name: Action vs. motion (Dramatistic distinction)
ontologyNodes.definition: Any verb with connotations of consciousness or purpose falls under 'act'; stumbling over an obstruction is not act but mere motion; the basic Dramatistic unit is 'the human body in conscious or purposive motion.' Behaviorism truncates drama by reducing action to motion. The watershed-moment dividing dramatist from operationalist vocabularies (GM-06): no instrument can record action ('ideas') except insofar as the subject-matter is reduced to motion.

ontologyNodes.name: Symbolic action
ontologyNodes.definition: Language considered as a mode of action (poetic) rather than information (scientific); a poem is the symbolic act of its maker, which the reader re-enacts in reading. Symbolic action is the realm of the incipient/attitudinal par excellence — actual conflicts can be transcended there, with results sometimes fatal, sometimes felicitous. Burke's central concept for analyzing literary works and rhetorical performances as motivated acts.

ontologyNodes.name: Incipient act / attitude (proto-sixth-term)
ontologyNodes.definition: An incipient act is a perception/attitude that contains the form of a not-yet-actualized act — Richards' 'preliminary adjustments, getting ready to act' or Mead's 'beginnings of acts.' Fundamentally ambiguous: an attitude can be SUBSTITUTE for an act OR FIRST STEP toward an act. Forward-anchors the sixth pentad term Burke adds in the 1962 Addendum (GM-09) and develops fully in A Rhetoric of Motives (1950). Keats's Urn-as-'fair Attitude' is the summational lyric instance.

ontologyNodes.name: Featuring of a term (philosophic-school diagnostic)
ontologyNodes.definition: Burke's diagnostic move: each philosophic school selects one of the five terms as Ausgangspunkt (generating principle) and develops a vocabulary suited to give that term full expression, with the other four slighted or placed in its perspective. Materialism features Scene; Idealism features Agent; Realism features Act; Pragmatism features Agency; Mysticism features Purpose. The diagnostic is featuring, not exclusivity — every philosophy deploys all five terms.

ontologyNodes.name: Grammar vs. philosophic idiom (universal vs. open)
ontologyNodes.definition: Burke's signature two-level claim: a statement of the grammatical principles of motivation can lay claim to universal validity (every motive-attribution must reference some background, etc.), but the choice of any particular philosophic idiom filling in those principles (God / nature / history / means of production for Scene) is open to question and varies with cultural situation. A philosophy is a casuistry of the pentadic resources.

ontologyNodes.name: Transformation of terms (master dialectical apparatus)
ontologyNodes.definition: Master apparatus of GM-09 and pervasive throughout the Grammar: tracking the disposition and trans-position of terms across motive-statements; the way ancestral, derivative, and bridge terms migrate, merge, split, or get re-keyed under dialectical pressure. Burke's signature methodological move — pentad as a generating principle whose transformations, permutations, and combinations produce the full variety of motive-statements.

ontologyNodes.name: Merger and division
ontologyNodes.definition: The two fundamental dialectical operations (Plato, Phaedrus): merger = comprehension of scattered particulars in one idea; division = carving an idea at the joints. Most concrete dialectical events are mergers atop division or divisions atop merger; a 'third / pontificating term' (continuity, polarity, synthesis) is usually generated to mediate. Per genus et differentiam is the classical instance: merger via genus + division via differentia.

ontologyNodes.name: Dialectic of the scapegoat
ontologyNodes.definition: Three-step ritual by which a charismatic vicar absorbs and carries off the collective iniquities of a community: (1) original merger — iniquities shared between iniquitous and chosen vessel; (2) ritualistic division — alienation of the shared element onto the vessel; (3) new merger — purified community defined in dialectical opposition to the sacrificial offering. The scapegoat is consubstantial with persecutors. Hitlerite Anti-Semitism is the cleanest negative example; Socrates as scapegoat of transcendence is the closing application.

ontologyNodes.name: Temporizing of essence
ontologyNodes.definition: The pun on sequence: the logically prior can be expressed as the temporally prior, and vice versa. Essence becomes narrated as a 'going back' to origins (Freud's primal horde, Plato's Meno-recollection, original sin); historicist and essentialist vocabularies are convertible. Translation rule: when an apparently empirical-historical claim is discredited as fact, ask whether it was really a statement about essence. Ibsen's Peer Gynt is GM-09's worked case.

ontologyNodes.name: Socratic transcendence (Upward Way)
ontologyNodes.definition: The upward dialectical move: a new motive discovered en route; the position at the end is reached by transformation, and the position at the start can only retrospectively be seen in light of the new motivation. Burke's signature reading: a Platonic dialogue is an ACT of transcendence (Phaedrus' five levels), not just a plea for one. Plotinus's journey 'to the Primal-Principle' is the mystical instance; Korzybski's higher-and-higher levels of generalization is the modern semantic instance.

ontologyNodes.name: Pentad overlap / common ground / margins of transformability
ontologyNodes.definition: The five pentad terms participate in a common ground or substance, whose role as their causal ancestor makes them transformable into one another at every point where their fields overlap. The 'great central moltenness' / alchemic alembic figure (GM-00): distinctions arise from a central moltenness where all is merged. The fingers-and-palm metaphor: terms distinct at the extremities merge in the palm of the hand. This pliancy is what licenses grand-style metaphysical reduction-to-one (being / action / motion as titular over-all terms).

ontologyNodes.name: Ambiguity as resource (not defect)
ontologyNodes.definition: Burke's methodological signature: where logical positivism and symbolic logic seek terms free of ambiguity, the Grammar wants terms that clearly reveal the strategic spots at which ambiguities necessarily arise, because the areas of ambiguity are exactly where transformations among the terms take place. Ambiguities are alchemic opportunities, not defects.

ontologyNodes.name: Consistent / compensatory points of departure
ontologyNodes.definition: A pentad term used as 'principle' admits two opposite developmental directions. Consistent: derive consequences from the term's nature ('reasons by a therefore'). Compensatory: depart toward the term's near-antithesis ('reasons by a however'). Lets a thinker keep a god-term while diverging from it ('naturalism' begun as man-in-nature becoming name for technology-and-money).

ontologyNodes.name: God-term
ontologyNodes.definition: A high-abstraction summarizing word — 'honor,' 'liberty,' 'Providence,' 'Absolute Idea' — gathering a complex of material conditions under a single spiritualized label. In RM-05, the apex term that ranks all other motives in an ultimate vocabulary. In RM-07, the terminus of dialectical ascent: from positive words, through titles, to title-of-titles. Burke's inventory lists substance, nature, history, society, logos, hierarchy, authority, consubstantiality, nation, freedom, pure persuasion as surrogate god-terms.
ontologyNodes.text: Burke - A Grammar of Motives; Burke - A Rhetoric of Motives

ontologyNodes.name: Ground (background / reason double-usage)
ontologyNodes.definition: The philosophical term 'ground' carries the double sense of background (scene) and reason (cause). Hegelian idealism exploits this by positing Reason as the Grundprinzip — at once mover of history and substance of which history is made. Leveraged in GM-10's reading of the theological controversy about whether God willed the good because it is good, or the good is good because God willed it.

ontologyNodes.name: Pathetic fallacy / motion-action ambiguity (extended)
ontologyNodes.definition: Ruskin's term (attribution of human emotions to non-human objects: 'the trees were gay, the mountains mourned') interpreted by Burke as tracking the scene-agent (or LYRIC) ratio. Burke extends to cover the broader 'action-motion ambiguity' (motion-personalization-as-act): 'the wheat tossed in the wind' is motion; 'the wheat tossed its head in the wind' is action. The watershed moment dividing dramatism from operationalism.

ontologyNodes.name: Poiema / pathema / mathema (tragic-dialectic triad)
ontologyNodes.definition: Burke's Greek-grammar triplet of action / suffering / learning. Greek proverb ta pathemata mathemata ('the suffered is the learned'). The tragic pattern: action (poiema) calls forth a counter-assertion from its context that the agent suffers (pathema); from the suffered comes knowledge (mathema) that transcends the original act. Christian martyrdom: act-of-self-sacrifice identical with sufferance; pathema (temptation) + poiema (resistance) + mathema (understanding) = martyrdom as new action-passion level.

ontologyNodes.name: Edenic paradigm (total acts producing total transformations)
