ontologyNodes.definition: If an agent acts in keeping with his nature (act-agent), changing his scene (scene-act), and likening agent to scene (scene-agent), the result is a state of mutual conformity — an Edenic paradigm applicable only to total acts producing total transformations. Theological notions of creation and re-creation approach this limit (Striegel's reading of Christ's work on the Cross; Aeschylus' Erinyes becoming Eumenides).

ontologyNodes.name: Demonic trinity (erotic + urinary + excremental cluster)
ontologyNodes.definition: Burke's image-cluster for the cloacal-mystical: three bodily principles vicariously substitutable for one another (rain ↔ urination ↔ erotic-purpose); 'thinking of the body' as condition of poetic transcendence; ecclesia super cloacam. Mystic thoroughness requires recognition of fundamental taboos at the very moment of their transcendence.

ontologyNodes.name: Dissolution of drama (four ways)
ontologyNodes.definition: The dramatistic perspective contains a point at which it abolishes itself in its own enunciation. Four canonical paths: (1) drama dissolves into lyric state; (2) action reduced to motion (scientism); (3) philosophies OF dramatism — Burke's own move — coordinates derived from drama yet used non-dramatically; (4) philosophies of super-drama — monotheistic god as super-person becomes impersonal.

ontologyNodes.name: Identification
ontologyNodes.definition: Burke's master term for rhetoric: A is identified with B when their interests are (or are persuaded to be) joined, making them consubstantial while each remains a distinct locus of motives. Replaces 'persuasion' as the governing term because it captures the intermediate rhetorical area between full deliberateness and full unconscious expression. Encompasses property-identification, autonomous-specialty identification, self-address, faction belonging, and ultimate mystical union as species.

ontologyNodes.name: Consubstantiality / Consubstantiation
ontologyNodes.definition: The substance-theoretic ground of identification: to identify A with B is to make them 'substantially one' while each remains a distinct locus. Grounded in the claim that 'substance' was originally an act — a way of life is an 'acting-together' in which people share sensations, concepts, images, ideas, and attitudes that make them consubstantial. Extended across units from person/person to person/faction, person/class, actor/universal-developmental-principle, and finally mystical union.

ontologyNodes.name: Attitude (Incipient Act) — 6th Dramatistic Term
ontologyNodes.definition: Burke's seeding of a sixth dramatistic term beyond the Grammar's pentad. Rhetorical language is inducement to action 'or to attitude, attitude being an incipient act' (p.42). A leaning or orientation that is not yet overt conduct; more general and foundational as a rhetorical target than action itself. In its mystic culmination (RM-07), all nervous impulses 'attitudinally glow' simultaneously — the pure incipience of ultimate identification.

ontologyNodes.name: Mystery
ontologyNodes.definition: The rhetorical condition arising where different kinds of beings communicate across a structural social divide. Requires both strangeness and the possibility of communion; generated by any pronounced social distinction — rank, class, age, race. Not subjective feeling but an objective structural effect of hierarchic difference. Ranges from embarrassment and glamour through military-caste aura to theological opacity. At its limit (RM-07), identification pushed absolutely becomes mystical.

ontologyNodes.name: Hierarchy
ontologyNodes.definition: The eulogistic word for bureaucracy and the universal motivational-symbolic principle organizing existence on a scale of higher/lower. Inevitable in systematic thought; reversible at the level of pure principle. Generates courtship, mystery, and mystification as its systematic effects. In RM-05, hierarchy becomes the formal structure of an 'ultimate vocabulary' — the guiding-idea or principle of principles that ranks competing dialectical voices.

ontologyNodes.name: Courtship
ontologyNodes.definition: The rhetorical principle operative whenever beings of different social kinds communicate; rhetoric generated wherever hierarchy structures relations. Not primarily sexual but structural — uses mystery's opacity as its suasive resource. Ranges from Castiglione's classical paradigm through Kafka's grotesque caricature to Kierkegaard's perpetual courtship (renunciation and advance fused in one attitude). The abstract paradigm of all persuasion when hierarchy is present.

ontologyNodes.name: The Negative
ontologyNodes.definition: Division as the ironic counterpart of identification — 'rhetoric is concerned with the state of Babel after the Fall' (p.23). Identification is affirmed with earnestness precisely because there is division; pure identification would eliminate strife. The negative also structures: the Kill and victimage (hierarchy generates guilt that seeks discharge), mystification (the specific concealed by the generic), and dialectical terms whose meaning shifts by contrast.

ontologyNodes.name: Pure Persuasion
ontologyNodes.definition: The limit-concept of rhetoric: the saying of something for a satisfaction intrinsic to the saying, not for extraverbal advantage. Exists nowhere in absolute form but is present as a motivational ingredient in any rhetoric. Its formal hallmark is self-interference or standoffishness: a persisting persuasive act requires its own self-interference, because when the plea is answered persuasion ends. Culminates dialectically in prayer as pure beseeching addressed to the god-term itself.

ontologyNodes.name: Terministic Screen
ontologyNodes.definition: Each vocabulary order constitutes a screen directing and deflecting attention: positive screen is physicalist/perceptual; dialectical screen is partisan/polar; ultimate screen ranks motives hierarchically. Switching screens changes what counts as a motive. First operative (unnamed) in RM-00's imaging-of-transformation analysis; named and systematized in RM-03's terministic-reservation and fully theorized in RM-05's three-vocabulary-orders framework.

ontologyNodes.name: Ultimate Identification
ontologyNodes.definition: The apex of the identification arc: identification pushed to its dialectical limit becomes mystical union — dissolution of the individual into boundless being, consubstantiality with the universal order. Characterized by William James's composite mystic portrait as the motive heading in 'God as the beloved cynosure and sinecure, the end of all desire' (p.333). Distinguished from Ersatzmystik (substitute mysticisms) that deform the same drive into demonic purpose.

ontologyNodes.name: Imaging of Transformation
ontologyNodes.definition: Transformation is the ground-motive; killing/suicide/self-immolation are one family of available images for localizing it. Includes Upward/Downward Way, Exile/Homecoming, seasonal cycles as equally valid alternatives. The specific image chosen is a terministic screen revealing motivational character.

ontologyNodes.name: Motivational Recipe
ontologyNodes.definition: The total complex of motivational ingredients in their proportions and contextual qualifications. Cannot be reduced to a single 'gist' without misrepresenting the whole. The qualifying modifiers supplied by dramatic context are themselves constitutive of the motive as a whole.

ontologyNodes.name: Dramatic and Philosophic Terms for Essence
ontologyNodes.definition: Narrative/temporal translation of philosophical essence-claims: the end of a story formally declares essence. Opposed to but formally homologous with philosophic terms (entelechy, abstract finishedness); mutually convertible by heuristic reversal. Includes temporizing of essence (ancestral or culminative pole).

ontologyNodes.name: Rhetoric as Addressed (incl. Self-Address)
ontologyNodes.definition: Persuasion implies an audience; a man can be his own audience ('an I addressing its me,' Mead). The psyche is a parliament; socialization presses from without while the individual completes it from within. 'Only those voices from without are effective which can speak in the language of a voice within' (p.39). Rhetoric's realistic function — inducing cooperation in symbol-responsive beings — is grounded here.

ontologyNodes.name: Formal Appeal
ontologyNodes.definition: The persuasive power of rhetorical form as such, independent of propositional content. Purely formal structures arouse collaborative expectancy in audiences, priming assent to whatever content occupies the formal slots. Form is itself a rhetorical motive, not mere embellishment.

ontologyNodes.name: Image as Identification-Node
ontologyNodes.definition: The image is 'built of identifications' (p.85): it condenses multiple organizing principles simultaneously, so translating an ideological argument into an image yields an 'unearned increment' of associated meaning — consubstantiality not explicitly contracted in the argument. Image and idea are continuous, both serving identification.

ontologyNodes.name: Imagination (Rhetorical Function)
ontologyNodes.definition: Genealogical treatment from Aristotle through Bacon to Hazlitt. Imagination as the immediate spring of action and ground of identification through anticipatory proximity: we identify more readily with what we can imaginatively inhabit. Rhetoric applies reason to imagination to move will (Bacon).

ontologyNodes.name: Triplicate Vocabulary (Bentham)
ontologyNodes.definition: Every domain of motive yields a neutral term flanked by eulogistic and dyslogistic counterparts. The neutral ideal is never a rhetorical reality; uninflected vocabulary cannot induce action. The eulogistic/dyslogistic poles are the normal condition of motivated discourse. Includes the censorial appellative — a word carrying evaluative weight as though descriptive.

ontologyNodes.name: Covering Motive (tegumen / res tegenda)
ontologyNodes.definition: When the actual motive behind an act cannot be presented eulogistically, a speaker selects the most favorable co-operative motive and presents it as the whole or essence. The linguistic veil (tegumen) over the interest concealed (res tegenda). Links Bentham's vocabulary analysis to Burke's theory of identification.

ontologyNodes.name: Mystification
ontologyNodes.definition: The rhetorical operation (Marx's dyslogistic term) by which specific class interests are concealed beneath apparently universal or spiritual motive-terms. The ideological substitution of generic for specific. Paired against Carlyle's eulogistic 'mystery': both address the same social phenomenon (hierarchy generating rhetorical difference) from opposite evaluative stances.

ontologyNodes.name: Imitation
ontologyNodes.definition: The master dramatistic concept subsuming competition, emulation, and the invidious; makes for consubstantiality by community of ways. Competition = out-imitation. The symbolic motive is more general than the pecuniary; laws of symbols are prior to any particular property structure. Veblen's 'invidious' is a partisan special case.

ontologyNodes.name: Administrative Rhetoric
ontologyNodes.definition: Rhetoric that includes nonverbal, material operations — spectacles, military force, institutional apparatus — as well as verbal address. Nonverbal conditions persuade by their symbolic meaning, not merely material effect. Burke's reading of Machiavelli's Prince as a manual of administrative rhetoric is the worked example.

ontologyNodes.name: Socioanagogic Method
ontologyNodes.definition: Secular adaptation of the medieval anagogical sense: reading social hierarchy where divine or erotic imagery appears on the surface. Positioned midway between Marx's rage at mystification and Carlyle's adulation of mystery. Treats a text's known moral/social judgments as transparent to disclose the hierarchic content of its imagery.

ontologyNodes.name: Three Vocabulary Orders (Positive / Dialectical / Ultimate)
ontologyNodes.definition: Positive terms: names grounded in perception, locatable hic et nunc (Bentham's real entities). Dialectical terms: polar vocabulary whose meaning shifts by contrast (Bentham's fictitious entities). Ultimate terms: a guiding-idea or principle of principles that places competing dialectical voices in a developmental hierarchy. Conflating the orders produces terministic impropriety; rhetoric operates primarily at the dialectical and ultimate levels.

ontologyNodes.name: Marxist Persuasion (as Ultimate Vocabulary Case Study)
ontologyNodes.definition: Burke's primary case study in ultimate vocabulary. Rhetorical power derives from arranging classes in a developmental hierarchy grounded in the universe itself, enabling any local participation to be simultaneously particular and universal (Hegelian concrete universal). The worker identified with 'the Proletarian' participates in the total dialectic of historical development.

ontologyNodes.name: Mythic Ground
ontologyNodes.definition: Motivational level transcending discursive reason, figured in image rather than idea. In Platonic dialogue, the culminating mythic image figures a motive the dialectical ascent has prepared one to receive. Mannheim's error is treating mythic ground as equivalent to ideological bias; doing so eliminates the primary motive power along with the biases.

ontologyNodes.name: Sociology of Knowledge (Mannheim)
ontologyNodes.definition: Mannheim's 'relationist' project: systematic discounting of ideological bias by studying connections between ideologies and their nonverbal conditions. Burke classifies it as 'pro-ultimate' — more precise than relativism but unable to reach genuine ultimate order because it lacks a governing principle of principles.

ontologyNodes.name: Embarrassment and Glamour
ontologyNodes.definition: Involuntary self-constraint triggered by hierarchic difference (embarrassment) and the quasi-magical perceptual magnification produced by hierarchic radiance (glamour — from 'gramarye,' necromancy). Both are evidence of mystery in social intercourse: the sign of different social kinds in contact.

ontologyNodes.name: The Kill / Victimage
ontologyNodes.definition: The mechanism by which hierarchy discharges the guilt it generates: invidious distinction produces accumulated moral pressure, discharged through scapegoating a sacrificial victim. The Kill is not the essence; common participation in a solemn experience is. The Rattlesnake Club anecdote is the paradigm: boys bonded by a shared notable experience, quickly fracturing into hierarchic cliques.

ontologyNodes.name: Range of Mountings
ontologyNodes.definition: Ideal paradigm for the symbol of ascending: kinesthetic, erotic, maternal, social-careerism, ethical, fecal-scatological, anagogic, and mystical-absolute strands. Maximum symbolic vibrancy obtains when all strands are simultaneously operative in a single symbol. Burke applies this to Hopkins, Yeats, Eliot, and Dante's Purgatorio.

ontologyNodes.name: Principle of the Oxymoron
ontologyNodes.definition: The mystic communicates in the oxymoron because mystic experience is the simultaneous glow of contradictory impulses — a condition of radical passivity in which all nervous impulses 'attitudinally glow' at once without the repression required for ordinary purposive action. The oxymoron is the literary analogue of this non-repressive condition.

ontologyNodes.name: Homo Dialecticus
ontologyNodes.definition: Man as the 'classifying animal' whose formal aptitude for classification is prior to social classification; social hierarchy is a special case of this general formal ground. Contrasted with homo faber (tool-using). Grounds Burke's argument that psychoanalytic and institutional explanations conceal the formal/dialectical priority.

ontologyNodes.name: Grammar–Rhetoric–Symbolic Triad
ontologyNodes.definition: Burke's three-volume architecture: Grammar built on 'substance' (universal paradoxes/placement); Rhetoric on identification ('substance' applied to persuasion/dissuasion); Symbolic to be built on 'identity' (unique individuals at peace). Consubstantiality bridges Grammar to Rhetoric; identification bridges Rhetoric to Symbolic.

ontologyNodes.name: Magic as Primitive Rhetoric / Faulty Derivation
ontologyNodes.definition: Word-magic reverses the true order: the realistic use of addressed language to induce action in people was mistakenly transferred to induce motion in things; magic is a faulty derivation from rhetoric, not its ancestor. Magic's socializing aspect is better read as 'primitive rhetoric' promoting social cohesion (Malinowski, Kluckhohn).

ontologyNodes.name: Advantage / Agonistic Rhetoric
ontologyNodes.definition: Burke's proposed master-term for subsuming all classical variants of rhetorical purpose and scientific psychological terminologies of drives. Rhetoric shaped by a strongly competitive purpose: proving opposites, countering jest with earnest. Related to Aristotle's view of rhetoric as 'the faculty of discovering persuasive means in a given case.'

ontologyNodes.name: Literature for Use
ontologyNodes.definition: Literary works performing rhetorical-political work: overtly (Areopagitica) or at one remove (Samson — ritual and magic order). Demonstrates that the range of rhetoric extends from bluntest propaganda through courtship, etiquette, education, sermon to 'pure persuasion' — appeal enjoyed for its own sake.

ontologyNodes.name: Rhetorica Utens / Rhetorica Docens
ontologyNodes.definition: Standard scholastic distinction: rhetoric comprises both the USE of persuasive resources (rhetorica utens, Demosthenes) and the STUDY of them (rhetorica docens, Aristotle's Art of Rhetoric). Burke uses this pair to define rhetoric's scope before expanding it through identification.

ontologyNodes.name: Context of Situation (Malinowski)
ontologyNodes.definition: Nonverbal situational factors that participate in a rhetorical act's effectiveness. Generalizes the requirement that meaning cannot be separated from nonverbal scene. Applied in RM-03 to qualify the Marxist diagnostic (terministic reservation) and in RM-05 to demonstrate that even positivistic reduction contains a minimal mythic element.

ontologyNodes.name: Mitsein / Being-with-one-another
ontologyNodes.definition: The political-rhetorical community presupposed by every speech act. Gross at Intro p. 11: 'it is in Aristotle's Rhetoric that Being-with, koinōnia, is given its definitive form.' Struever names alltägliches Miteinanderreden (everyday speaking-with-one-another) as the primary structural mode Heidegger thematizes in GA 18 155. Michalski reads GA 18 as Heidegger's interpretation of concrete Dasein as Miteinandersein via the basic possibilities of speaking-with-one-another (Miteinandersprechen, GA 18 110). Kisiel makes Mitsein the rudimentary ground of his rhetorical protopolitics; Hyde anchors enthymeme's audience-completion on the Mitsein-soil. Pöggeler reads BT §29's claim about rhetoric as 'first systematic hermeneutic of everydayness of being-with-one-another' as the moment when the political is confined to everydayness (das Man), thereby restricting rhetoric's deliberative-public scope.

ontologyNodes.name: Befindlichkeit / Attunement
ontologyNodes.definition: Heidegger's BT §29 term, identified across the volume with Aristotelian pathos via GA 18 122 ('these pathē are not psychological states; they are a Befindlichkeit of the living one in his world'). Michalski makes Befindlichkeit the philologist's mode of attuned-and-comprehending being-in-the-world (befindlich-verstehendes In-der-Welt-sein, p. 75). Gross argues BT's Befindlichkeit narrows GA 18's pathos by stripping out the political-rhetorical dimension (HR-01-GROSS-B-P8: BT 344, BT 434 'rarefied domain of resolute Freeman'). Pöggeler reads pathos = Befindlichkeit as the substitution that constitutes the restriction of rhetoric in BT. Hyde aligns Stimmung/Befindlichkeit with pathē in the call-of-conscience reading (BT 179-182, 228-235, 342). Struever uses dispositions as her preferred English rendering.

ontologyNodes.name: Alltäglichkeit / Everydayness
ontologyNodes.definition: Volume-central term whose contested translation marks the Gross/Struever continuity reading vs. Pöggeler restriction reading. Struever titularly insists Alltäglichkeit means 'timefulness' (her coined term against 'ordinariness') — the catalytic agent of temporality and the primary qualification of Miteinandersein (p. 105-115). Gross reads it as the everydayness that BT 178 names rhetoric the 'first systematic hermeneutic' of. Michalski links it to Heidegger's 'as anyone' (als Man / das Man, p. 76). Pöggeler reads BT §29's confining-the-political-to-everydayness as the restriction-move that surrenders the deliberative-public dimension of rhetoric to das Man.

ontologyNodes.name: Phronēsis / Practical Wisdom
ontologyNodes.definition: Aristotle NE VI virtue, central to four contributors. Gross reads phronesis as the Vico-Gadamer-Heidegger recovery against Cartesian-Kantian intellectualization. Gadamer: 'Phronēsis is a whole virtue; it is not an ability, but a being' (Ch 2 p. 61); phronesis is hexis, not technē. Hyde activates the etymological link phronesis-phrēn (heart) and cites Taminiaux 1992 (p. 141): Heidegger said 'phronesis is Gewissen [conscience] set in motion which makes an action transparent (durchsichtig).' Kisiel reads phronesis as the action of resoluteness receptive to call of conscience; Heidegger's 1933 'will' is conditioned wholly in terms of Aristotelian phronesis grasping kairos. Pöggeler: 1922 Natorp-Bericht characterization of phronesis as Gewissen is the conceptually decisive move that channels rhetorical-pathic into existential-ethical register.

ontologyNodes.name: Dynamis / Power-Capacity
ontologyNodes.definition: The volume's signature Aristotelian correction. Three contributors (Gadamer, Struever, Kisiel) explicitly defend the GA 18 114 dictum that rhetoric is dynamis, not technē (Aristotle Rhet. 1355b25-26: dynamis tou theoresai, 'capacity for theorizing what is persuasive in a given case'). Gadamer makes this the central rhetorical-philosophical question of his interview (Ch 2 §II): 'Heidegger said the technē-designation is incorrect, whereas dynamis is the correct definition.' Struever specifies dynamis tou theoresai as the precise Aristotelian phrase (Rhet. 1355b26 / GA 18 122) and reads it as the temporal-incompleteness that makes rhetoric the proper instrument for politics. Kisiel: rhetoric is 'first of all not an art but a power, dynamis ... cultivated power of situational insight, phronesis' (p. 146). Volume-tension VT2: dynamis vs. technē.

ontologyNodes.name: Kairos / Timely Moment
ontologyNodes.definition: Five contributors invoke kairos as the rhetorical-temporal moment Heidegger develops via GA 18. Gross: 'a decisive moment (krisis) that folds past experience and future possibilities into a provisional present' (Intro p. 33-37). Struever: 'meson für die praxis ist der kairos' (GA 18 144); meson defined as Jeweiligkeit (temporal particularity), 'rarely translated into Greek' but central to Heidegger's account of Aristotelian Grundbegriffe (p. 110-126). Kisiel: kairos as 'the moment of decision in polity/policy' = the speaker's resoluteness brings others to same resolution (p. 146). Hyde: anger collapses imagined future revenge into present immediacy (Rhet. 1378b3-5) — pathos's kairos-restructuring of temporality.

ontologyNodes.name: Sorge / Care
ontologyNodes.definition: BT's signature structural concept (§§39-44). Listed by Gross as a key BT term descending from SS 1924 rhetorical-Aristotelian apparatus (Intro p. 2, n.5-7). Struever uses Sorge in BT-cite mode (p. 120); Besorgen (concern / care-taking-of) is Heidegger's term for practical concern, which Struever links to kairos (GA 18 140). Cross-pipeline link to BT D2.

ontologyNodes.name: Call of Conscience
ontologyNodes.definition: Hyde's titular concept, structurally central to his epideictic-conscience reading. BT §§54-60: the silent call (BT 318: 'conscience discourses solely and constantly in the mode of keeping silent') as ontologically-prior showing-forth (epideixis) of the heart of human existence. Hyde's signature thesis: the call IS a primordial form of epideictic rhetoric. Cited approvingly by Gross (Intro p. 2) and Kisiel (p. 146: ethos translated into Entschlossenheit = receptive response to call of conscience). Pöggeler reads BT §§54-60 as the moment where rhetoric is LOST, not preserved (P2 targets Hyde directly).

ontologyNodes.name: Fundamental Ontology
ontologyNodes.definition: Heidegger's titular project in BT. Gross's signature claim: 'Heidegger thus relocates rhetoric at the heart of his fundamental ontology' (Intro p. 4) — the volume's load-bearing centrality thesis (HR-01-GROSS-A-P2). 'Rhetorical ontology' (Gross's coining) is fundamental ontology approached through its discursive-existential medium. The thesis directly targets the conventional separation of rhetoric (as merely a sub-discipline) from ontology (as foundational). Pöggeler's countertitle (HR-07-POGGELER-P1) directly opposes: rhetoric is NOT a constitutive concept of fundamental ontology; it is restricted to the Marburg lectures.

ontologyNodes.name: Epideictic Rhetoric
ontologyNodes.definition: Aristotle's third rhetorical genre (Rhet. I.3) alongside deliberative (sumbouleutikon) and judicial (dikanikon). Hyde radicalizes the genre ontologically: epideictic is the showing-forth (epideixis) of what is, especially of the existential structure of the heart. The call of conscience is THE primordial epideictic event (HR-04-HYDE-P1). Gross briefly: 'the rhetoric of praise and blame, or epideictic, gets short shrift in Heidegger's course, as it does in Aristotle's text' (Intro p. 10-11). Kisiel reads Heidegger's May 26, 1933 Schlageter speech as an instance of epideictic operating politically (p. 135-136).

ontologyNodes.name: Deliberative Rhetoric
ontologyNodes.definition: Aristotle's first rhetorical genre (Rhet. I.3). Per Gross's reading of GA 18: the genre that 'allows an advocate addressing a political assembly to characterize a problem, lay out concrete possibilities for future action, and forge a common opinion regarding what is to be done' (Intro p. 11, citing GA 18 124-125). Volume-cross-pipeline tension VT10: Heidegger himself foregrounds deliberative rhetoric in GA 18 §§13-14 (BCAP unit U-FP3a), while Hyde imports the epideictic emphasis.

ontologyNodes.name: Kinēsis / Being-moved
ontologyNodes.definition: Gross's subtitular concept and Struever's structural foundation. Heidegger's GA 18 288: 'Die kinesis ist eine Weise des Seins des Daseienden selbst' (motion is a mode of the Being of Dasein itself), reading Aristotle Physics 202b23. Gross: kinesis defined by interanimation of pathetikos (passive-undergoing) and poietikos (active-making); the German middle voice operationalizes this. Struever's signature SS 1924 syllogism: 'If life, then motion, kinēsis. If motion, then time' — kinesis 'gives the authentic Da-Charakter to Dasein, the vital place-time of Being' (p. 106-109). Pöggeler reads kinesis = poietikon + pathetikon at the close of GA 18 as 'the conceptual track for BT's poiesis-emphasis' — the moment pathos is sidelined into Befindlichkeit/Stimmung. Cross-pipeline tension VT12.

ontologyNodes.name: Doxa
ontologyNodes.definition: Six contributors invoke doxa. Gross reads Heidegger's doxa (GA 18 149-151) as 'pretheoretical being-for' — 'authentic being-with-one-another in the world' (eigentliche Entdecktheit des Miteinanderseins-in-der-Welt), characterized by yes-saying-without-examination (Ja-sagen, GA 18 136-137) and openness (Es könnte auch anders sein). Struever: doxa is 'the way we have life in time, Alltäglichkeit' (GA 18 138); endoxa are revisable rhetorical premises. Hyde reads doxa as authentic discoveredness of Mitsein. Kisiel develops doxa twofold (via Arendt): opinion + splendor/fame (dokein = Ansicht + Ansehen) — the space of appearance.

ontologyNodes.name: Zoon Politikon / Zoon Logon Echon
ontologyNodes.definition: Aristotle's twin defining-concepts of human Dasein (Politics I.2). Struever: 'Grundcharakter des Daseins als zōon politikon' (GA 18 104) — human life defined by possession of language (logon echon); life fulfilled by language-use (zoē praktikē meta logon, GA 18 105). Kisiel: zōon logon echon now in textual register of newspapers (modern Dasein as newspaper-reader, p. 132) — three Aristotelian definitions read by Heidegger as equally primordial. Gross: zōon politikon implicit in Mitsein/koinonia framework (Intro p. 11).

ontologyNodes.name: Sprachlichkeit / Linguisticality
ontologyNodes.definition: Gadamer's titular concept for Ch 2 Section IV. The medium 'in which mortals live in the speaking of language' (n. 17, citing 'Die Sprache' 1950). Not nominalistically reducible to words: 'pointing is also already language and the whole body speaks too' (book p. 59). 'Everything that can allow something to be understood. Therefore, hermeneutics; thereby its indefinability' (p. 60). 'Linguisticality is only an approximating concept' (p. 59). Gadamer subsumes Sprachlichkeit under rhetoric ('rhetoric is the overarching concept for everything that has to do with the other,' p. 60).

ontologyNodes.name: Hermeneutics of Facticity
ontologyNodes.definition: Heidegger's pre-BT methodological term (GA 63, SS 1923). Gross: the rhetorical genealogy of BT terms 'historicizes' the hermeneutics of facticity that 'predated SS 1924 by at least two years' (Intro p. 2). Gross-B: Luther's Affektenlehre (per Dockhorn) 'opens the way for what would later become the hermeneutics of facticity practiced by both Heidegger and Gadamer.' Michalski: the precondition for hermeneutic phenomenology proper (BT 1927).

ontologyNodes.name: Hermeneutic Phenomenology / Philology
ontologyNodes.definition: Michalski's titular thesis. Heidegger 'rejects the title of philosophy in favor of philology even for this region that exceeds the horizon of classical philology' (p. 72). Philology = 'passion for the knowledge of that which has been expressed and of its self-expression' (Leidenschaft der Erkenntnis des Ausgesprochenen und des Sichaussprechens, GA 18 4, 333). Philology is the necessary element of hermeneutic phenomenology that takes account of the leading function of speech (logos) in the dominance of the interpretedness of Dasein. Hermeneutic phenomenology = Heidegger's recasting of Husserl's reflexive phenomenology by appropriation of fore-having/fore-seeing/fore-grasping. Volume tension VT7: phenomenology vs. philology, resolved synthetically by Michalski.

ontologyNodes.name: Rhetorical Protopolitics
ontologyNodes.definition: Kisiel's titular thesis (Ch 6): the rudimentary politics taking shape in Heidegger's emerging fundamental ontology of 1923-24, where the everydayness of being-with-one-another (a speech-community whose telos is Verständigung) sediments a 'politics' equiprimordial with rhetoric. Speech-as-political. Not full political philosophy but the protopractical layer that frames the speech-situation as already political. Distinct from but congruent with Struever's 'politics of time' (p. 124) and Gross's 'rhetorical pluralism' (Intro V).

ontologyNodes.name: Topology of Being
ontologyNodes.definition: Pöggeler's titular countertitle and structural opposite to Gross's 'rhetorical ontology.' Heidegger's mature post-1947 concept (Aus der Erfahrung des Denkens; Heidegger's Dec 12, 1958 letter to Pöggeler): 'the literal speaking of place,' 'thinking the truth' as 'the disclosure of the self-concealed (Entbergen des Sichverbergens) of being.' The place-figure that supplants both metaphysical essence-articulation and the Marburg Aristotelian-rhetorical engagement. Crystallized in the Geviert (fourfold). Heidegger 'in this term ... was not aware of historical connotations' (i.e., rhetorical topics-tradition) — explicit disavowal of rhetorical genealogy. Kisiel's third polis-concept (archaic-poietic, 1935-43) covers the same textual territory but with opposite valence.

ontologyNodes.name: Hexis / Settled Disposition
ontologyNodes.definition: Aristotelian NE II concept, central to Struever's reading and Gadamer's phronesis-doctrine. Struever: hexis is the Grundbestimmung of aretē (GA 18 185); 'a potential for having; not pure duration but timebound, acquired and lost.' Hexis is dynamis, Gefasstsein (185). 'Hexis is ein Wie des pathos' (GA 18 184) — habit is a mode of pathos, the dispositional ground that makes kairos-grasp possible. Gadamer (Kemmann framing, n. 27 = GA 18 165): 'The interaction with the pathē is a question of hexis: ethos and pathē are constitutive of legein itself.'

ontologyNodes.name: Middle Voice
ontologyNodes.definition: Gross's signature stylistic-philosophical concept. The Greek-grammatical voice that expresses simultaneity of activity and passivity, which Heidegger reproduces in German via morphological play (bewegen-bewegt-Bewegung morphology, es gibt impersonal, 1959's 'die Sprache spricht'). For Gross, the central stylistic-philosophical resource by which Heidegger operationalizes Being-moved (HR-01-GROSS-A-P6). Distinguished from Derrida's differance/mouvance reading (which 'neutralizes' rather than 'interanimates' active/passive). 'Heidegger's middle voice in no way kills the author. Rather it describes in new terms how the author is rhetorically constituted' (p. 24).

ontologyNodes.name: Affektenlehre / Doctrine of Affections
ontologyNodes.translation: doctrine of affections / theological-rhetorical pathos tradition
ontologyNodes.definition: Gross-B's signature genealogical bridge. The Christian-theological transformation of Aristotle's pathē running from Augustine, Damascenus, Gregory of Nyssa, pseudo-Dionysius, through medieval Thomas, to Luther. Per Dockhorn: Luther's Affektenlehre 'grounds Enlightenment philosophy' and opens 'the way for what would later become the hermeneutics of facticity practiced by both Heidegger and Gadamer.' The genealogical bridge from Aristotle through Christian theology to Heidegger SS 1924. Struever notes the Patristic-medieval-Stoic Affektenlehre tradition (n. 22).

ontologyNodes.name: Trope
ontologyNodes.definition: Gross's revisionary account of Heidegger's elocutio-equivalent. 'A trope, acting in concert with its staid manifestation as a concept (Begriff), marks the contours of contingency' (Intro p. 3). Tropes 'provide the nontheoretical distance necessary to see how we are in our everyday situations and how we are moved.' Distinguished from Nietzsche's 'originary' tropes and from rhetoric-as-ornament. The trope/concept dyad is constitutive, not decorative.

ontologyNodes.name: Restricted Conception of Rhetoric
ontologyNodes.definition: Pöggeler's titular thesis. 'Restricted' = BOTH temporally bounded (Heidegger's rhetoric engagement is circumscribed to the Marburg lectures 1923-28) AND substantively curtailed (Heidegger 'restricted crucial dimensions of Aristotle's Rhetoric on the path to Being and Time' — failing to ask after justice; relegating pathos to Befindlichkeit; surrendering rhetoric to the 'they'). The volume's countertitle: Pöggeler closes the volume by problematizing its opening centrality claim.

ontologyNodes.name: Disclosedness / Unconcealment
ontologyNodes.definition: Heidegger's BT term for the manner in which Dasein and beings are revealed. Struever: GA 18 138 ('doxa is the way we have life in time'); doxa as authentic Entdecktheit of Miteinandersein. Kisiel: pistis equiprimordial with aletheia (Section V titular thesis); three modes of concealment / three modes of trueing, two of which Heidegger attributes to language of rhetoric (p. 144-148). Pöggeler: late Heidegger reads truth as 'unconcealment' from 'strictly non-Platonic and non-metaphysical standpoint,' yet (per Ijsseling) the concept 'adheres strictly to the ancient Greek understanding of language' — the rhetorical tradition hidden but persistent.

ontologyNodes.name: Anyone / Das Man / Publicness
ontologyNodes.definition: BT §27 existentiale. Kisiel: das Man = 'true bearer of the universal of averageness = our language' (GA 18 64); 'domineering prevalence of Anyone in language = doxa, the tacit major premises of rhetoric.' Hyde insists Heidegger has BOTH a negative pole and a positive pole: 'publicness belongs to Dasein's positive constitution' (BT 167). The positive pole authorizes rhetorical work of orator who modifies public moods. Pöggeler: Heidegger 'treats publicness only as the mode of being for the they' — the restriction of the political-deliberative to inauthentic everydayness.

ontologyNodes.name: Jeweiligkeit / Temporal Particularity
ontologyNodes.definition: Struever's signature temporal translation. 'Meson für die praxis ist der kairos' (GA 18 144); 'meson is Jeweiligkeit (temporal particularity — particular while) in respect to the agent' (GA 18 201). Michalski: Heidegger refuses 'each' (jedes) as standard rendering for hekaston; 'Hekaston means what in each case obtains [Jeweiliges] insofar as I linger with it' (GA 18 32). Kisiel: 'temporally particularizing universals' (jeweilige Universalia) — peculiarly temporal universals sensitive not only to distributive each (jede) but also to varying temporal contexts (je nach dem).

ontologyNodes.name: Phobos / Fear
ontologyNodes.definition: Volume-central pathos illustration. Gross-B's signature reading (Section IV): fear as relational-temporal Befindlichkeit (GA 18 256-257); fear's structural feature is Möglichkeit / Möglichsein; most fearsome = the Reserved (Zurückhaltenden) and Ironic (Ironischen) (GA 18 257). Fear is 'Befindlichkeit that brings into speech' (GA 18 261). Struever: phobos has 'peculiar tense, voice, and mode' — future tense, voice subjunctive, mode the possible (GA 18 246-263). 'Phobos bouleutikous poiei — fear makes us deliberators' (Rhet. 1383a6-8). Hyde: BT §30 fear (180-182). Pöggeler reads Augustinian timor castus/timor servilis distinction as Christian-theological scaffolding under Heidegger's fear-analysis.

ontologyNodes.name: Showing-forth / Aufzeigen / Sage
ontologyNodes.definition: Hyde's structural bridge between Aristotelian epideixis and Heideggerian Aufzeigen. Heidegger's recurrent gloss of language as a 'showing' — early BT and later Sage — operates 'in the same structural register' as Aristotle's epideixis (the act of epideictic). 'To speak means to say, which means to show and to let [something] be seen' (Zollikon Seminars 215). Aligns Heideggerian 'showing-forth' with Aristotle's epideixis.

ontologyNodes.name: Pisteis / Three Modes of Persuasion
ontologyNodes.definition: Aristotle Rhet. I.2's three pisteis. Kisiel's central Section V thesis: the three pisteis (pathos, ethos, logos) are close kin to three modes of disclosedness of human situation (Befindlichkeit/Verstehen/Rede). Equiprimordiality, convertibility, interchangeability. GA 18 165: 'ethos and pathos are constitutive for legein itself.' Hyde works with the three modes throughout. Struever: 'Rhetoric 2: creation/alteration/reception of doxa, endoxa, pathē, prohairesis, pisteis, krisis exhausts limited repertoire of political acts.'

ontologyNodes.name: Player Involvement Model (PIM)
ontologyNodes.definition: Calleja's volume-level frame: a 6-dimensional grid of involvement axes (kinesthetic, spatial, shared, narrative, affective, ludic) cross-cut by a macro/micro temporal-phase distinction, organized as layered and transparent rather than discrete.

ontologyNodes.name: Involvement (umbrella analytic)
ontologyNodes.definition: The pre-immersive category of player engagement Calleja uses as the spine term — genus of which incorporation is the intensified species; analytic prerequisite to presence/immersion and itself resting on attention.

ontologyNodes.name: Incorporation
ontologyNodes.definition: Calleja's titular replacement frame: the most intensified and internalized blending of PIM dimensions, gated by a spatial+kinesthetic cornerstone and a simultaneity condition; structurally bidirectional (player absorbs the environment AND is absorbed into it); preserves both 'absorption' and 'transportation' senses of immersion in an expanded double-axis.

ontologyNodes.name: Macro temporal phase
ontologyNodes.definition: Off-line involvement with the game: pre-session and post-session thinking, planning, anticipation, community participation, motivation to return; the longer-term contextualization of the moment of gameplay.

ontologyNodes.name: Micro temporal phase (in ludo res)
ontologyNodes.definition: In-session, moment-to-moment engagement during the act of play; ergodically active in the dispositional sense; attentionally structured by the same six dimensions on a finer temporal grain.

ontologyNodes.name: Three-tier attentional hierarchy (attention → involvement → presence/immersion)
ontologyNodes.definition: Calleja's stratification of player-experiential categories: attention is the precondition of involvement; involvement is the precondition of presence/immersion. The lower stratum must be modeled before the higher can be analyzed.

ontologyNodes.name: Family-resemblance methodology (Wittgensteinian)
ontologyNodes.definition: Calleja's volume-level methodological signature, iteratively applied at three levels: at IG-01 to game-definition (vs. essentialism); at IG-03 to PIM dimensions as overlapping/non-essential axes; at IG-10 to incorporation as family-resemblance of experiential modes.

ontologyNodes.name: Virtual environment habitation
ontologyNodes.definition: The surviving spatial-phenomenological metaphor after the demolition of presence/immersion: the player's sense of inhabiting an on-screen place rather than perceiving a representation of space; the master metaphor of the spatial dimension and the load-bearing trope of the incorporation thesis.

ontologyNodes.name: Alterbiography (emergent player-narrative)
ontologyNodes.definition: Calleja's term for the ongoing emergent autobiographical story of a player-character (or focalized entity / miniature) constituted through the player's interaction with the game world's embedded objects, inhabitants, and events; complement to (not opponent of) scripted narrative.

ontologyNodes.name: Ergodicity as dispositional readiness to act
ontologyNodes.definition: Calleja's reformulation of Aarseth's ergodic input: ergodic effort is first and foremost a dispositional readiness to act, not merely the physical pressing of buttons; cognitive effort and patient alertness count as ergodic.

ontologyNodes.name: Internalization (of attentional load / controls / space / shared involvement)
ontologyNodes.greek: of attentional load / controls / space / shared involvement
ontologyNodes.definition: Process by which a learned task becomes automatic and ceases to consume the limited attentional resource, freeing capacity for other dimensions; paradigmatic at kinesthetic control-learning but operative for spatial place-internalization and shared involvement too.

ontologyNodes.name: Cybernetic circuit / cybernetic feedback loop
ontologyNodes.definition: Dovey + Kennedy 2006 figure for the player-machine loop: hardware + representational layer + rules + environment constitute a feedback circuit within which ergodic input takes effect; in IG-08 expanded to a cognitive + emotional + kinesthetic feedback loop.

ontologyNodes.name: Spatial+kinesthetic cornerstone of incorporation
ontologyNodes.definition: Calleja's gating condition for incorporation: spatial and kinesthetic involvement together are the necessary minimum substrate; without inhabited place and embodied control there is no incorporation. The kinesthetic→spatial dependency is the structural ground (you must move to inhabit).

ontologyNodes.name: Double-axis structure / bidirectional metaphor of incorporation
ontologyNodes.definition: Incorporation operates along two simultaneous axes: the player absorbs the virtual environment into consciousness AND the player's avatar is absorbed into the virtual environment. Replaces immersion's unidirectional plunge with a reversible bidirectional figure.

ontologyNodes.name: Simultaneity condition for incorporation
ontologyNodes.definition: The temporal-axis gate on incorporation: dimensions must operate at sustained intensity simultaneously (not serially); incorporation is sustainable-but-fleeting and its intensity is proportional to duration.

ontologyNodes.name: Experiential gestalts (Lakoff+Johnson via Calleja)
ontologyNodes.definition: Lakoff+Johnson 2003 experientialist construct imported in IG-10 as the philosophical anchor for incorporation: metaphor is constitutive of cognition, not a deviation; experience is structured by holistic gestalts grounded in bodily lived-experience.

ontologyNodes.name: Subjective distance (player ↔ game environment)
ontologyNodes.definition: The experiential variable the book theorizes: its shortening yields the sensation of inhabiting on-screen space. Proto-formulation of the bidirectional incorporation later articulated in IG-10.

ontologyNodes.name: Four conceptual challenges of presence/immersion
ontologyNodes.definition: Calleja's canonical enumeration in IG-02: (1) absorption-vs-transportation conflation; (2) ergodic-vs-non-ergodic media difference; (3) technological/fidelity determinism; (4) monolithic-perspective (immersion treated as single binary phenomenon). The destination Calleja's PIM and incorporation must answer.

ontologyNodes.name: Avatar anchoring + system reactivity (structural differentia)
ontologyNodes.definition: Calleja's structural specification of what makes game-environment presence different from non-game-media presence: the player is anchored via an avatar and the system reacts to player input in nontrivial, ergodic ways. The differentia that motivates a game-specific PIM.

ontologyNodes.name: Symbolic / mimetic / symbiotic control continuum
ontologyNodes.definition: IG-04's primary typology of kinesthetic control mapping (Figure 4.3): symbolic (button-to-meaning, abstract); mimetic (gesture-replicates-action); symbiotic (player and game co-extended through internalized control). The chapter's load-bearing innovation in kinesthetic operationalization.

ontologyNodes.name: Agency (Murray/Schott vs. Giddens/capability)
ontologyNodes.definition: Calleja's contested concept-bundle: Murray (1998) + Schott (2006) frame agency as satisfaction in seeing the result of one's decision; Calleja partially displaces this in favor of Giddens's agency-as-capability and Mateas+Stern's local/global agency. The chapter is the book's primary agency theorization.

ontologyNodes.name: Contingency (Malaby — performative + social)
ontologyNodes.definition: Malaby 2007's claim that contingency is constitutive of games (not incidental); Calleja deploys it across IG-04 (contrivance of contingency / performance / risk-of-failure) and IG-06 (social contingency codependent on performative contingency).

ontologyNodes.name: Five-structure spatial taxonomy (Calleja)
ontologyNodes.definition: Calleja's substitute for Nitsche's labyrinth/tracks-and-rails distinction: five spatial structures — unicursal corridor / labyrinth, multicursal corridor / maze, rhizomatic zone, open landscape, arena. Augmented by miniature and tactical spaces. The chapter's load-bearing typology.

ontologyNodes.name: Cognitive mapping / mental cartography
ontologyNodes.definition: Tolman 1948 via Golledge+Garling 2004: the player's construction of internal spatial models across nested scales (landmark + wayfinding + body-relative orientation + imageability). The cognitive substrate of spatial involvement.

ontologyNodes.name: Space → place transition (Tuan)
ontologyNodes.definition: Tuan 1977's familiarization-yields-place schema, adopted by Calleja as the experiential mechanism by which navigable space becomes inhabited place — the spatial-internalization analog of kinesthetic-control-internalization.

ontologyNodes.name: MMOGs as third places / on-line societies
ontologyNodes.definition: IG-06's central social-theoretic frame, importing Oldenburg's third-place concept via Steinkuehler + Williams: MMOGs are full-fledged on-line societies better at bridging than bonding social capital; governance, reputation, and persistent social bonds operate at MMOG scale.

ontologyNodes.name: Cohabitation / cooperation / competition (three-not-four shared subtypes)
ontologyNodes.definition: Calleja's three modalities of shared involvement, including ambient awareness of social context. The 'three-not-four enumeration slip' surfaced in IG-06 as a notable internal-text inconsistency.

ontologyNodes.name: Human-vs-AI co-agent distinction
ontologyNodes.definition: IG-06's position that player disposition is fundamentally restructured by perceived human-vs-AI status of co-agents — even rudimentary AI grounds cohabitation, but only persistent human-controlled agents support the reputation-and-betrayal layer (EVE Online Guiding Hand exemplar).

ontologyNodes.name: Scripted narrative vs. alterbiography (co-constitutive)
ontologyNodes.definition: Calleja's narrative-theoretic move that dissolves the narratology-vs-ludology binary: scripted narrative (designer-installed story-elements) and alterbiography (emergent player-narrative) are co-constitutive of narrative involvement, not mutually exclusive.

ontologyNodes.name: Push narrative vs. pull narrative
ontologyNodes.definition: Calleja's analytic distinction between designer-pushed scripted progression and player-pulled emergent-narrative pursuit — the dispositional reorientation that determines focalization and story-time/discourse-time interplay.

ontologyNodes.name: Excitatory homeostasis + rhetorical strategies of affect
ontologyNodes.definition: Bryant+Davies 2006 media-psychology frame, central to IG-08: affect is the emotional-tonal modulation of involvement generated via the cognitive+emotional+kinesthetic feedback loop, ranging across calming/adrenaline/uncanny. Designed and player-precipitated affect both count.

ontologyNodes.name: Escapism vs. escape (round-trip vs. one-way)
ontologyNodes.definition: Calleja's defense of escapism via Tolkien (Escape of the Prisoner vs. Flight of the Deserter): escapism is a legitimate round-trip imaginative activity that returns to the everyday, distinct from one-way escape. Imagination is the human faculty enabling escapism; secondary worlds (Tolkien 1983) are its habitable form.

ontologyNodes.name: Strategy / tactics / microtactics three-tier hierarchy
ontologyNodes.definition: Calleja's IG-09 analytic innovation: strategies = plans in pursuit of primary goals; tactics = plans in pursuit of subgoals; microtactics = plans during moment of action. The three-tier hierarchy tracks goal-tier and temporal-distance and is the ludic dimension's load-bearing typology.

ontologyNodes.name: Goal-source taxonomy (system / self / community)
ontologyNodes.definition: Calleja's three-way classification of goal-origin: game-stipulated, player-stipulated, community-stipulated. Refuses both Suits's lusory-attitude single-source goal-genesis and McIntosh's claim of universal primary-goal concreteness in games.

ontologyNodes.name: Magic-circle excision
ontologyNodes.definition: Calleja's deliberate exclusion of the Huizinga/Salen+Zimmerman/Juul magic-circle concept on two grounds: spatial redundancy (in digital games only navigable virtual space can be acted in) and empirical absence (no game-specific experiential bracketing in his interview data). One of three excisions structuring IG-03.

ontologyNodes.name: Lusory-attitude excision
ontologyNodes.definition: Calleja's refusal of Suits's lusory-attitude criterion (voluntary adoption of inefficient rule-restricted means) on two grounds: digital games enforce rules mechanically (no voluntary adoption needed) and Suits's argument is circular.

ontologyNodes.name: Fun-essentialism excision
ontologyNodes.definition: Calleja's rejection of the fun=games equation on two grounds: fun imposes a normative status that ignores variation across players' experiential states (including MMOG labor/tedium per Steinkuehler, Yee, Dibbell) and is analytically empty as a category.

ontologyNodes.name: Grounded-theoretic qualitative methodology (WoW + Planetside)
ontologyNodes.definition: Calleja's three-year qualitative research design: extended personal participation in WoW (Blizzard 2004) and Planetside (SOE 2003), 25 in-game semi-structured interviews (two 2-hour sessions, in-game), focus groups, forum monitoring, blog tracking, machinima review; iterative coding generates the six dimensions as clusters of emphasis. The dissertation's empirical-adaptation seed.

ontologyNodes.name: KINESTHETIC involvement
ontologyNodes.definition: Engagement with avatar / game-piece control, spanning from conscious learning of the controls to fluent internalized movement; foregrounded when controls 'make themselves present' through unmastery or complex-sequence demand. The ergodic-dispositional substrate of the other dimensions.

ontologyNodes.name: SPATIAL involvement
ontologyNodes.definition: Engagement with spatial qualities of a virtual environment via spatial control, navigation, and exploration; the internalizing of game-space such that the player senses inhabiting a place rather than perceiving a representation of space.

ontologyNodes.name: SHARED involvement
ontologyNodes.definition: Engagement with awareness of and interaction with other agents (human- or computer-controlled) under modalities of cohabitation, cooperation, and competition; encompasses guild-political deliberation, ambient social-context awareness, and the human-vs-AI distinction.

ontologyNodes.name: NARRATIVE involvement
ontologyNodes.definition: Engagement with both story-elements scripted into the game and emergent stories generated by ongoing interaction with the game world, its embedded objects, inhabitants, and events. Dissolves the narratology-vs-ludology binary via the scripted/alterbiography co-constitution.

ontologyNodes.name: AFFECTIVE involvement
ontologyNodes.definition: Engagement with emotional states elicited by play — from calming aesthetic response through adrenaline-rush arousal to action-horror uncanny — including both designer-installed rhetorical strategies of affect and player-precipitated affective interpretations.

ontologyNodes.name: LUDIC involvement
ontologyNodes.definition: Engagement with choices and their repercussions across game-stipulated, player-stipulated, and community-stipulated goals; opportunity cost is constitutive of well-balanced ludic systems — without repercussions, actions lose meaning.

ontologyNodes.name: uncomfortable situation
ontologyNodes.definition: Titular load-bearing category: a situation in which one's habituated emotional repertoire fails to fit the predicament, exposing the rhetorical-constructive layer of emotion; cognition 'practically situated but uncomfortably so.'

ontologyNodes.name: rhetorical ontology of emotion
ontologyNodes.definition: Gross's methodological signature: emotion is not biologically hardwired nor purely socially constructed but rhetorical-situated — emerging from negotiated transactions among organism, environmental affordances, and discursive frames; rhetoricity is a methodological strength.

ontologyNodes.name: situated conceptualization (Barsalou-Barrett)
ontologyNodes.definition: Cognitive-science paradigm (Wilson-Mendenhall et al. 2011) in which emotion concepts are instantiated in context-dependent, audience-inflected scenarios — settings, agents, objects, events, interoceptions — rather than retrieved from amodal taxonomies; the volume's invitational scientific bridge.

ontologyNodes.name: negative / hostile / rhetorical affordance
ontologyNodes.definition: Gross's Gibsonian extension: an environmental offering whose threat- or promise-character is constituted not by direct perception but by language- and narrative-mediated rhetorical situations; abandons Gibson's invariance criterion to admit historically-conditioned hostile environments.

ontologyNodes.name: hostile environment
ontologyNodes.definition: Titular concept of Ch.3 (Radcliffe): an environment whose affordances are constitutively negative-but-not-merely-dangerous, requiring rhetorical/narrative analysis beyond physical risk; legally instantiated in 'hostile workplace' protected-class categories; cf. race-based slavery as environment (Ch.2).

ontologyNodes.name: prosthetic emotion
ontologyNodes.definition: Mode 4 of the typology (Susan Miller / Cynthia Haynes 'pathos@play.prosthetic.emotion'): the object or scene extends our emotional range; someone or something suffers in our stead (Passion of Christ; 'Jesus loves you'). Equiano's bearing-the-cross-for-Jesus is the chapter-length demonstration; the Imitation of Christ four-mode reading is the Intro exemplar.

ontologyNodes.name: seven-mode rhetoric-of-emotion typology
ontologyNodes.definition: Gross's signature taxonomy (Intro pp.10-11): mimetic, cathartic, projective, prosthetic, performative, voluntary, systematic. Replaces the hardwired/constructed binary and provides the analytic toolkit deployed across chapters.

ontologyNodes.name: bearing up
ontologyNodes.definition: Ch.2 titular concept: Equiano's rhetorical-emotional disposition under slavery — carrying / sustaining (OED 'bear' I–II + 21) under conditions in which the bearer is excluded from the social-recognitional structures that would normally make endurance intelligible. Neither stoic endurance nor pragmatic adjustment; at the limit, borne by Christ.

ontologyNodes.name: mixed feelings (anti-Galenic)
ontologyNodes.definition: Ch.4 titular concept: not internal proportional mixtures of stable basic emotions (Galenic humours, Ekman blending) but socially-negotiated convergences of conflicting reference values on character; prefigures Kahneman-Tversky prospect theory and indexes Barrett-Barsalou situated conceptualization.

ontologyNodes.name: irreconcilable difference / two cultures
ontologyNodes.definition: Epilogue titular framework (after C. P. Snow 1959 Rede Lecture): the sciences-vs-humanities chasm. The volume answers Snow's question with a qualified No — the dichotomy DISSOLVES (not resolves into a third response) when emotion is studied as a rhetorical-situational phenomenon.

ontologyNodes.name: comfort (as bourgeois keyword)
ontologyNodes.definition: After Moretti's *The Bourgeois*: comfort shifts in the late 17th / early 18th c. from a return to normality after adversity to taking normality as starting point and pursuing well-being as an end in itself (Robinson Crusoe 1719 transitional). Anchors the eighteenth-century 'critical history of well-being.'

ontologyNodes.name: negation as rhetorical-emotional engine
ontologyNodes.definition: Across-chapter rhetorical operator: affirmative through negation of contrary (litotes; double negative). Sterne's 'fear not, envied not' (Sentimental Journey 120) and Austen's 'no unhappy reverie' (Emma 321) / 'Not no feelings' (S&S) flout Grice's Maxim of Manner to flag stereotype-violation; Adeline's nonreferring 'undone' is the Gothic analogue.

ontologyNodes.name: rhetorical situation (Bitzer, extended)
ontologyNodes.definition: Lloyd Bitzer 1968 — exigence + audience + constraints. Gross recasts exigence as 'basic discomfort' and rehabilitates Bitzer (Ch.3) as proto-affordance theory; bridges to Burke's 'literature as equipment for living' and Aristotle's Rhetoric II as the earliest negative-affordance treatise.

ontologyNodes.name: basic emotions / Ekman program
ontologyNodes.definition: Ekman's evolved-for-adaptive-value basic-emotion list (anger, fear, disgust, surprise, joy, sadness, contempt) + FACS coding + Pictures of Facial Affect; the volume's principal scientific antagonist, glossed as 'impoverished Darwinianism' that strips Darwin's interpretive openness.

ontologyNodes.name: complex states of mind (Darwin)
ontologyNodes.definition: Darwin's term (Expression p.260) for emotions — envy, jealousy, suspicion, conceit, devotion, maternal love (p.82) — not revealed by fixed expression; requires literary-humanistic methodology (Shakespeare's 'green-eyed monster'; Spenser's 'foul ill-favoured'). The Darwin-as-rhetorician evidence base.

ontologyNodes.name: Cognitive Approaches to Literature (CAL) — contested
ontologyNodes.definition: Subfield (Howard, Crane, Thrailkill, Keen, Zunshine, Vermeule) importing Ekman-Damasio-LeDoux infrastructure into literary criticism; Gross's recurring strawman across chapters — proceeds 'unecologically toward theory of mind,' produces diminishing returns, forecloses cultural-rhetorical analysis.

ontologyNodes.name: Literary Darwinism / evocriticism — contested
ontologyNodes.definition: Brian Boyd, Pinker, Carroll, Dutton — 'cheesecake for the mind' applications of evolutionary psychology to literary criticism. Gross identifies affirming-the-consequent + undistributed-middle fallacies and a 'six red flags' diagnostic (Pleistocene, modularity, neuron etc.).

ontologyNodes.name: creditable emotion (Williams)
ontologyNodes.definition: Raymond Williams's term (*Long Revolution* p.321): an emotion functioning as lived reference point even though it contradicts the conditions for its own satisfaction — exemplified by 'feeling of freedom carefully controlled' in late liberal democracies. Gross's lever against Massumi's pre-ideological affect.

ontologyNodes.name: Hegelian strand in Merleau-Ponty
ontologyNodes.definition: Gross's Ch.2 interpretive claim: Merleau-Ponty's 'Freedom' chapter (Phenomenology of Perception p.84) — 'my human situation abolishes my biological one' + three-page Marxist footnote 172n1 — contains a Hegelian-Marxist line that Dreyfus's pragmatic-phenomenological reading systematically loses.

ontologyNodes.name: vested interests (Carretta)
ontologyNodes.definition: Carretta's biographical formulation re-deployed analytically: the owner has vested interest in slave well-being; the overseer does not; and a freed black in a race-based-slavery environment finds no one with vested interest in his well-being — making Equiano paradoxically more secure as a slave. Distinguishes interest from felt attachment.

ontologyNodes.name: spiritual autobiography / Mount Calvary unsealing
ontologyNodes.definition: Genre frame for Equiano's conversion narrative (*Narrative* 189-190): four-step allegorical structure (godly sadness → rebirth → challenge → manifestation). The scriptures become an 'unsealed book'; executes Gross's analytic point that Equiano cannot bear himself — only Christ bears. Prosthetic-emotion's central in-text demonstration.

ontologyNodes.name: Lewinian Gestalt apparatus
ontologyNodes.definition: Kurt Lewin's Gestalt-psychological field-theory terms imported by Gross: Aufforderungscharakter / valence (invitation-character of environment), Umstrukturierung (field-transformation), Aus-dem-Felde-Gehen (leaving the field), Umweltkrafte (fields of force), 'hopeless situation' (1935, p.94 — child encysts self in inescapable predicament).

ontologyNodes.name: paradiastole (redescription)
ontologyNodes.definition: Renaissance rhetorical figure (Peacham; Quentin Skinner): naming a vice as virtue (or vice versa) by redescription, arguing *in utramque partem*. Gross identifies it as Radcliffe's signature trope ('care, or rather, the neglect, of strangers') and deploys it across chapters; the perlocutionary engine of the rhetorical affordance.

ontologyNodes.name: Gothic sentimental subgenre
ontologyNodes.definition: Walpole-Lewis-Radcliffe generic complex (Castle of Otranto, The Monk, Romance of the Forest) where the cause of death and the terms of a life-undone find genre-form because emotional scenes pose real threat. Antonia's 'undone' (The Monk) is the chapter's emotional-rhetorical thesis-statement-in-miniature.

ontologyNodes.name: Kahneman reference-value / prospect-theory framework
ontologyNodes.definition: Kahneman-Tversky prospect theory + Kahneman-Miller 1986 'Norm Theory' (counterfactual availability, emotional amplification, perceived abnormality) + Kahneman 1992 'Reference Points, Anchors, Norms, and Mixed Feelings' + hedonic treadmill (Brickman et al.). Austen prefigures it; Equiano resists its scaling.

ontologyNodes.name: interested onlookers / situational ambiguity
ontologyNodes.definition: Gross's Ch.4 chapter-crux: Edward's mixed feelings are 'defined by interested onlookers who, in this case, include us' — Elinor, Marianne, Lucy, John Dashwood, Mrs. Jennings, the reader. Aligns with Barrett-Barsalou situated conceptualization (Jim Webb angry-or-elated). Onlookers establish reference values; situations themselves are ambiguous.

ontologyNodes.name: Phelps amygdala / Modern Racism Scale study
ontologyNodes.definition: Phelps et al. 2000 (J. Cog. Neuroscience 12.5, 729-738): fMRI of White American responses to Black/White faces; Exp.1 amygdala correlates with UNCONSCIOUS bias (not MRS) on unfamiliar faces; Exp.2 famous-positive faces (Arsenio Hall, MLK Jr.) fail to reproduce pattern. The Epilogue's chief test-object for rhetorical-situational reframing of neuroscience.

ontologyNodes.name: empathy / apathy / reticence triad
ontologyNodes.definition: Preston's signal Epilogue contribution: empathy is properly understood only with its negation (apathy) and the distinct third term reticence — quiet patients exhibiting minimal demonstrative emotion who appear to have deep emotions and need. Breaks the circularity of mirror-neuron accounts of empathy.

ontologyNodes.name: reverse inference (Poldrack)
ontologyNodes.definition: Poldrack 2006 (Trends in Cognitive Sciences): methodological problem in neuroimaging — inferring same cognitive process from same regional activation across studies; renders causal arguments suspect. Anchors the Epilogue's eight-point critique of fMRI/PET/TMS laboratory neuroscience (localization illusion, technocratic hierarchy, etc.).

ontologyNodes.name: queer phenomenology of comfort (Ahmed)
ontologyNodes.definition: Sara Ahmed *Queer Phenomenology* (2006): comfort, disorientation, alienation; whiteness as comfort; objects gather along certain lines; orientation depends on taking points of view as given. Methodological ally across the volume; 'amended' by Gross in Equiano chapter (Equiano pressed into service outside Ahmed's social-investment frame).

ontologyNodes.name: rhetorical-historical scaffolding (Griffiths-Scarantino)
ontologyNodes.definition: Paul Griffiths + Andrea Scarantino 'Emotions in the Wild' (2009): synchronic scaffolding (Vygotskian — confessional in church) + diachronic scaffolding (Catholic-cultural development of confession-capacity) + emotional capital; the 'wedding ceremony' framework. Gross critiques Barsalou's elliptical-figures limit ('and so forth') by recourse to this.

ontologyNodes.name: Afro-Pessimism (engaged not endorsed)
ontologyNodes.definition: Sexton, Wilderson, Moten — diagnosis of Black exclusion from systems of intelligibility ('not ever' admitted). Gross deploys it to underwrite Equiano's exclusion (litany of the inoperable: enslavement of progeny, inadmissibility of black testimony) while declining wholesale endorsement; retains rhetorical-humanities methodology.

ontologyNodes.name: racism located in institutions, not brains
ontologyNodes.definition: Gross's Epilogue signal claim: racism is located primarily in INSTITUTIONS (US race-based slavery, Jim Crow) that exceed any particular brain state, not in physiology. The Phelps amygdala-correlate makes sense only when reframed as a rhetorical-situational object referred to racist institutions; Gross's mediating field = critical race theory + rhetorical studies.

ontologyNodes.name: central historical claim (lab topics ↔ socio-historical concerns)
ontologyNodes.definition: Epilogue thesis: 'the topics of laboratory work on the emotional brain coincide meaningfully with particular socio-historical concerns that show up at the margins of experiment design and interpretation' — fear-research → post-war anti-racism; empathy-research → post-war humanitarianism. The methodological warrant for two-cultures collaboration.

ontologyNodes.name: indeterminacy as constitutive (Roughgarden / Darwin)
ontologyNodes.definition: Closing argument of Ch.1: semiotic indeterminacy is biologically constitutive, not maladaptive — Joan Roughgarden's *Evolution's Rainbow* 'balanced portfolio' of genes; Darwin's weeping-children plate (Ginx's Baby) as locus of constitutive indeterminacy; the work of triangulating 'is never done nor should it be.'

ontologyNodes.name: Aristotelian heritage (pathē / Rhetoric II)
ontologyNodes.definition: Continuous low-key background: Aristotle's *Rhetoric* Book II (pathē) as cast-of-characters specification of emotion in uneven social relationships; *Poetics* on cathartic transaction; pathos in the classical lexicon as 'positing a social relationship.' Indexed at pp.21, 40-41, 47, 69, 166n5.

ontologyNodes.name: embodied philosophy / phenomenological design thinking
ontologyNodes.definition: design as enacted theory; phenomenology as design thinking's next evolution (p.6 / pdf 8)

ontologyNodes.name: anti-Cartesianism
ontologyNodes.definition: dissolves self/world and mind/body; theory-practice and thinking-making dualisms are symptoms (p.22 / pdf 24)

ontologyNodes.name: ready-to-hand / present-at-hand continuum + breakdown
ontologyNodes.definition: withdrawn use vs detached deliberation; breakdown is revelatory (p.27 / pdf 29)

ontologyNodes.name: mediation as constitutive
ontologyNodes.definition: media co-constitute the real; amplify while reducing (p.96 / pdf 98)

ontologyNodes.name: Ihde's four mediation relations
ontologyNodes.definition: embodiment / hermeneutic / background / alterity (p.87 / pdf 89)

ontologyNodes.name: affordance + embodiment
ontologyNodes.definition: objects perceived by what they afford before naming; body as system of possible actions (p.130 / pdf 132)

ontologyNodes.name: sense vs meaning; meaning over utility
ontologyNodes.definition: sense=one context, meaning=sum of imaginable contexts; design meaning, not mere function (p.137 / pdf 139)

ontologyNodes.name: transparency, not invisibility
ontologyNodes.definition: perceived-through and re-enterable interface keeps the user active (p.146 / pdf 148)

ontologyNodes.name: problem-solution paradox
ontologyNodes.definition: problem and solution co-evolve; abduction; thinking-through-making; anti-waterfall (p.73 / pdf 75)

ontologyNodes.name: multistability & creative misuse; intention not primary
ontologyNodes.definition: tech is what it can do; outcomes emergent; design conditions of possibility (p.111 / pdf 113)

ontologyNodes.name: design as being-in-the-world / care
ontologyNodes.definition: design a modern mode of being-in-the-world (Mitcham); care designed into being (Fry); objects carry an ethics (p.12 / pdf 14)

ontologyNodes.name: thing / gathering (the jug's void)
ontologyNodes.definition: the thing 'things'; the immaterial shapes the designed; design intangible systems of meaning (p.118 / pdf 120)

ontologyNodes.name: technē / poiēsis / standing reserve / enframing
ontologyNodes.definition: Heidegger's technology essay; passivity risk of standing reserve (p.37 / pdf 39)

ontologyNodes.name: abduction / design thinking (4 parts)
ontologyNodes.definition: empathy/framing/ideation/validation; logic of what-could-be (p.62 / pdf 64)

ontologyNodes.name: craft vs design; the hand; un-throwing
ontologyNodes.definition: design is modern (division of labor); the hand makes+thinks; design as coping with thrownness (p.58 / pdf 60)

crossPipelineHooks.title: ψυχή (DA) → ζωή πρακτική (BCAP)
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: DA's faculty hierarchy (nutritive → sensitive → appetitive → locomotive → intellectual) maps onto BCAP's ontological interest in the *praktikē tou logon echontos* (the practical exercise of the being that has logos).
crossPipelineHooks.relevance: This hook grounds the argument that Aristotle's psychology is already proto-existential in its teleological structure.

crossPipelineHooks.title: φαντασία (DA) → Erschlossenheit / Being-in-the-World (B&T)
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: DA III.8's thesis that "the soul is in a way all existing things" (432a1--3) is a locus Heidegger repeatedly engages.
crossPipelineHooks.relevance: This hook is load-bearing for the dissertation's central argument.

crossPipelineHooks.title: αἴσθησις (DA) → Befindlichkeit (B&T)
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: The critical parallel lies in the *receptive* character of both *aisthēsis* and *Befindlichkeit*.
crossPipelineHooks.relevance: This hook supports the argument that *aisthēsis* is proto-attunement: an embodied, world-directed, receptive mode of being that discloses the environment's character through the organism's own structural calibration.

crossPipelineHooks.title: φάντασμα (DA) → Merkbild (Uexkull)
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: The structural parallel is precise: both *phantasma* and *Merkbild* are organism-internal perceptual residues that guide action in the absence of current stimulation.
crossPipelineHooks.relevance: This hook supports the argument that phantasia is the Aristotelian ancestor of the biosemiotic *Merkbild* -- but with a crucial ontological difference.

crossPipelineHooks.title: ὄρεξις + φαντασία → κίνησις (DA) → Ambient Rhetoric (Rickert)
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: The DA III.9--11 circuit (phantasia → orexis → kinēsis) is the Aristotelian mechanism by which appearances produce bodily movement through the mediation of desire.
crossPipelineHooks.relevance: This hook establishes that the phantasia-orexis-kinēsis circuit of DA III is the Aristotelian foundation for Rickert's ambient rhetoric.

crossPipelineHooks.title: αἴσθησις as Form-Reception (DA) → Weltarmut / Weltbildend (GA 29/30 via Uexkull)
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: DA's distinction between plant (affected by forms with matter = no perception) and animal (receives forms without matter = genuine perception) is a precursor to Heidegger's stone/animal distinction.
crossPipelineHooks.relevance: This hook positions the wax-signet principle as the Aristotelian version of the *Weltbildung* threshold.
