crossPipelineHooks.title: κίνησις in MA → BCAP on κίνησις [INTERP-high]
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: **Aristotelian concept**: κίνησις (C3) — animal locomotion as a specific instantiation of the general concept of movement; requires both an internal immovable point and an external immovable ground; caused proximately by desire.

crossPipelineHooks.title: φαντασία as practical mover → BCAP on φαντασία [INTERP-high]
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: **Aristotelian concept**: φαντασία (C2) — presents objects to desire as a "faculty of discrimination" (700b19-21); can produce involuntary movements "without express mandate of the intellect" (703b6-8); mediates between perception and action.

crossPipelineHooks.title: ὄρεξις and the practical syllogism → BCAP on ὄρεξις and πρᾶξις [INTERP-high]
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: **Aristotelian concept**: ὄρεξις (C1) as the proximate efficient cause of action; the practical syllogism (C4) as the logical structure of desire-driven action.

crossPipelineHooks.title: σύμφυτον πνεῦμα → Embodied action [INTERP-med]
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: **Aristotelian concept**: σύμφυτον πνεῦμα (I2) — the connate spirit as the bodily medium transmitting desire's motive force to the limbs through expansion and contraction.

crossPipelineHooks.title: The puppet analogy → Automaticity and ambient action [INTERP-med]
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: **Aristotelian concept**: The puppet (αὐτόματον) analogy — "the movements of animals may be compared with those of automatic puppets" (701b2); a tiny occasion sets off cascading movement.

crossPipelineHooks.sourceConcept: τὸ ἀγαθόν as final cause of movement
crossPipelineHooks.title: τὸ ἀγαθόν as final cause of movement → Teleological structure of action [INTERP-low]
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: **Aristotelian concept**: τὸ ἀγαθόν (C5) — the good (actual or apparent) as the final cause initiating desire and thus movement; "not every intelligible object, but only the end in the domain of conduct" (700b25).

crossPipelineHooks.title: χρῶμα → Sense and Sensibilia colour theory [INTERP-high]
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: **Aristotelian concept**: χρῶμα (C1) — simple colours derived from the four elements; intermediate colours from mixture and blending.

crossPipelineHooks.title: πέψις (maturation) → Biological teleology [INTERP-med]
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: **Aristotelian concept**: πέψις (C4) — the maturation process driving chromatic change in plants and animals through heat, nutriment, and moisture.

crossPipelineHooks.title: λευκόν as deviation/weakness → Privation ontology [INTERP-low]
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: **Aristotelian concept**: White as the colour of "deviation from natural colour" (798a25-b5), associated with weakness, ageing, and premature maturation.

crossPipelineHooks.title: Dyeing analogy → Techne and nature [INTERP-low]
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: **Aristotelian concept**: βαφή (I3) — dyeing as the paradigm case of colour transference; used as analogy for natural processes (fruit maturation, animal colouring).

crossPipelineHooks.title: φάντασμα as memory-image → B&T temporality [INTERP-high]
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: **Aristotelian concept**: φάντασμα (C3) — the dual-aspect memory-image that functions simultaneously as an object of contemplation in itself and as a likeness (εἰκών) of the thing remembered.

crossPipelineHooks.title: μνήμη / ἀνάμνησις → B&T retention and retrieval [INTERP-high]
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: **Aristotelian concept**: μνήμη (C1) as passive retention conditioned by time; ἀνάμνησις (C2) as active inferential recovery through sequential reactivation of movements.

crossPipelineHooks.title: ἀνάμνησις as ζήτησις → Rhetorical τόποι [INTERP-high]
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: **Aristotelian concept**: ἀνάμνησις operates through "places" (τόποι) — starting-points from which recollection proceeds by hunting up associations (similarity, contrariety, contiguity).

crossPipelineHooks.title: κίνησις (residual movements) → BCAP on κίνησις [INTERP-high]
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: **Aristotelian concept**: κίνησις (C5) — residual physiological movements left by perception; their sequential reactivation constitutes recollection; movements succeed one another by nature, custom, or association.

crossPipelineHooks.title: τὸ πρῶτον αἰσθητικόν (common sense) → Sense and Sensibilia [INTERP-med]
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: **Aristotelian concept**: τὸ πρῶτον αἰσθητικόν (I1) — the primary perceptive faculty / common sense, which cognizes time, magnitude, and motion; the organ to which memory essentially belongs.

crossPipelineHooks.title: τύπος (wax-seal model) → Embodied cognition [INTERP-med]
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: **Aristotelian concept**: τύπος (I3) — the impression stamped in the soul and its bodily seat; the wax-seal analogy (450a27-b1); physiological conditions (moisture, hardness) explain individual differences.

crossPipelineHooks.title: ψόφος / πληγή → De Anima II.8 sound theory [INTERP-high]
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: **Aristotelian concept**: ψόφος (C1) — all sounds arise from the impact (πληγή) of air against bodies; the De Audibilibus provides the detailed material acoustics.

crossPipelineHooks.title: σαφές (clearness) across modalities → Common sensibles and cross-modal analogy [INTERP-med]
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: **Aristotelian concept**: σαφές (C4) — clearness in sound analogous to clearness in colour; the claim that the strongest, purest stimuli produce the most distinct impressions across both modalities.

crossPipelineHooks.title: τραχύς (roughness) → Touch and cross-modal perception [INTERP-med]
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: **Aristotelian concept**: τραχύς (I2) — rough sounds arise when the impact is divided and dispersed, "each portion striking separately"; compared to rough objects touching the skin.

crossPipelineHooks.title: πνεῦμα (breath) → MA σύμφυτον πνεῦμα [INTERP-low]
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: **Aristotelian concept**: πνεῦμα (C3) — breath as the material cause of vocal sound; its force, quantity, and manner of expulsion determine vocal quality.

crossPipelineHooks.title: συμφωνία (concord) → Ratio-theory in De Sensu [INTERP-low]
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: **Aristotelian concept**: συμφωνία (I3) — musical concords arise from overlapping note-impacts causing intermediate sounds to escape notice.

tensionEdges.dependencyRelation: Rhetorical energeia presupposes metaphysical sense (activity/aliveness as mode of being)
tensionEdges.conflictRelation: Metaphysical sense is abstract and atemporal (priority thesis); rhetorical sense is concrete and perceptual (vividness)
tensionEdges.description: Whether the Rhetoric's energeia is a genuine application of the Metaphysics concept or a homonymous appropriation. The transfer from ontological priority to aesthetic vividness is Aristotle's most striking conceptual redeployment, and the mechanism of connection is never made explicit.

tensionEdges.nodeA: psyche (DA II.1: first entelecheia of natural body; inseparable from body)
tensionEdges.nodeB: nous (DA III.5: active nous is separable, immortal, eternal)
tensionEdges.dependencyRelation: Nous is a capacity of soul; hylomorphic definition should govern all psychic capacities
tensionEdges.conflictRelation: Active nous breaches the hylomorphic framework: separable, immortal, eternal (430a17-22)
tensionEdges.description: The fundamental tension of De Anima. The hylomorphic definition that governs all other psychic faculties is violated at the highest point. Reverberates into Met Lambda (divine self-thinking) and the theological tradition.

tensionEdges.nodeA: kinesis (Phys III.2: energeia ateles, incomplete actuality)
tensionEdges.nodeB: energeia (Met Theta.8: actuality prior in formula, time, substance)
tensionEdges.dependencyRelation: Physics definition deploys the actuality concept from Metaphysics Theta
tensionEdges.conflictRelation: Incomplete actuality is paradoxical within a framework where actuality = completion
tensionEdges.description: The central interpretive crux connecting Physics and Metaphysics. Whether kinesis constitutes a genuine third ontological category between potentiality and completed actuality, or is merely a conceptual device, remains the most debated question in Aristotle's process ontology.

tensionEdges.nodeA: phantasia (DA III.3: kinesis from actual sensation — causally derived)
tensionEdges.nodeB: phantasia (DA/Rhet/Mem/MA: functionally autonomous in dreams, deliberation, rhetoric, involuntary movement)
tensionEdges.dependencyRelation: Phantasia originates in sensation and inherits its reliability structure
tensionEdges.conflictRelation: A causally dependent capacity achieves operational independence across all four application domains
tensionEdges.description: Phantasia's causal derivation from sensation conflicts with its functional autonomy in four domains: dreaming (DA), rhetorical reception (Rhet pro ommaton poiein), memory retention (Mem phantasma as likeness), and involuntary physiology (MA blushing/trembling). How a dependent capacity achieves independence is raised but never resolved.

tensionEdges.nodeA: telos (Phys II.8: nature acts for an end without deliberating)
tensionEdges.nodeB: techne (Phys II.8: art acts purposively through deliberation)
tensionEdges.dependencyRelation: Teleological argument relies on art-nature analogy
tensionEdges.conflictRelation: Stripping deliberation while retaining purposiveness undermines the analogy
tensionEdges.description: Whether non-deliberative purposiveness is genuinely explanatory or covertly metaphorical. Extends to Movement of Animals where the practical syllogism compresses deliberative structure to vanishing point in rapid action.

tensionEdges.nodeA: practical syllogism (MA ch. 7: universal major + particular minor = action)
tensionEdges.nodeB: orexis (MA/DA: desire as proximate efficient cause of locomotion)
tensionEdges.dependencyRelation: The practical syllogism formalizes the desire-perception-action chain
tensionEdges.conflictRelation: The conclusion is an action, not a proposition; rapid-action cases compress deliberation to nothing
tensionEdges.description: Whether the practical syllogism is a genuine logical form or a psychological causal sequence dressed in logical language. Bridges logic and psychology in a way that threatens the integrity of both.

tensionEdges.nodeA: nous (DA III.4: impassible, unmixed, without nature of its own)
tensionEdges.nodeB: phantasma (DA III.7: the soul never thinks without an image)
tensionEdges.dependencyRelation: Nous depends on phantasmata for all operations
tensionEdges.conflictRelation: Phantasmata are bodily residues of sensation; nous is supposed to be free of bodily determination
tensionEdges.description: The wax-signet model applied to both sense and thought threatens to collapse the distinction between embodied perception and separable intellection. If nous genuinely requires bodily images, its separability claim is undermined.

tensionEdges.nodeB: to_agathon (Met Lambda.10: the good as both separate principle and immanent cosmic order)
tensionEdges.dependencyRelation: God's thinking is the supreme actuality; the universe's order depends on it
tensionEdges.conflictRelation: A self-thinking god has no cognition of the world he orders
tensionEdges.description: How a self-thinking god can govern worldly order without cognizing it. If God thinks only himself, the mechanism by which divine thought structures cosmic order is opaque.

tensionEdges.nodeA: eidos (Met Z.viii: man generates man — form shared across instances)
tensionEdges.nodeB: eidos (Met Z.xiii: no universal is substance — form must be individual)
tensionEdges.dependencyRelation: Form is substance; substance must be a 'this' not a 'such'
tensionEdges.conflictRelation: If form is numerically the same across instances it is universal; if numerically distinct, what individuates it?
tensionEdges.description: The fundamental tension of Metaphysics Z, never resolved. The Categories' treatment of individual composites as primary substance adds a further layer. Whether Aristotle's mature position is that individual forms are particular is one of the most debated questions in Aristotle scholarship.

tensionEdges.nodeA: chronos (Phys IV.11: number of motion — grounded in motion, mind-independent)
tensionEdges.nodeB: chronos (Phys IV.14: time qua numbered requires soul as counter)
tensionEdges.dependencyRelation: Time is defined through motion but counting requires psyche
tensionEdges.conflictRelation: Ambiguous ontological status: mind-independent or mind-dependent?
tensionEdges.description: Extends to On Memory where time is the necessary condition of memory and only time-perceiving animals can remember, binding physics to psychology. Aristotle hedges: motion can exist without soul, but time as numbered cannot.

tensionEdges.nodeA: rhetorike (Rhet I.1: morally neutral capacity that can be misused)
tensionEdges.nodeB: rhetorike (Rhet I.1: truth and justice are naturally stronger)
tensionEdges.dependencyRelation: Rhetoric is a genuine techne with systematic rational structure
tensionEdges.conflictRelation: Value-neutrality claim conflicts with truth-orientation; art-concealing-art deepens paradox
tensionEdges.description: The constitutive tension of the Rhetoric. If truth is naturally stronger, rhetoric should be superfluous; if rhetoric is needed, truth's natural strength is insufficient. The naturalness principle (art concealing art) makes the most truthful-seeming speech the most artfully constructed.

tensionEdges.nodeA: phantasma (Mem: object of contemplation in itself, theorema)
tensionEdges.nodeB: phantasma (Mem: likeness of the thing remembered, eikon)
tensionEdges.dependencyRelation: Memory consists in perceiving the phantasma qua likeness
tensionEdges.conflictRelation: The shift from in-itself to qua-likeness presupposes awareness of the absent original it explains
tensionEdges.description: The representational puzzle at the heart of Aristotle's philosophy of mind. How does the soul recognize a present image as a likeness of an absent thing without already having access to the absent thing? This is the Aristotelian anticipation of the modern problem of intentionality.
Readiness-to-hand is ontologically prior, yet presence-at-hand is what the tradition takes as the default mode of Being. The contrast is both structural and critical.
Das Man is a necessary existentiale, yet authenticity requires wresting oneself from it. Dependence + opposition = productive tension.
Disclosedness is Dasein's 'there,' but falling is equally constitutive and works against disclosure. The 'there' both reveals and conceals.
Care is the being of Dasein (Division One), but temporality reinterprets it at a deeper level (Division Two). The 'same' structure shifts meaning.
Death individualizes absolutely, yet Dasein is essentially Being-with. The tension between radical singularity and constitutive sociality is never fully resolved.
Within-time-ness is genuinely derived from originary temporality, yet it systematically conceals its own origin. Derivation + concealment.
Dasein is simultaneously thrown (already-in) and projecting (ahead-of-itself). These are co-original moments of care that pull in opposite temporal directions.
Dasein is its possibilities (existence) yet always already determined (facticity). Neither can be reduced to the other; their unity is care.
Assertion depends on interpretation but transforms it. The logical tradition mistakes the derivative for the primordial.

tensionEdges.text: Heidegger - Basic Concepts of Aristotelian Philosophy
tensionEdges.description: Movement IS the presence (ἐντελέχεια) of what is able to be there precisely insofar as it is not yet completed (ἐνέργεια). The equivocation is ontologically necessary.

tensionEdges.text: Heidegger - Basic Concepts of Aristotelian Philosophy
tensionEdges.description: Meaningfulness (Bedeutsamkeit) and potentiality are two faces of the same phenomenon. The world is encountered as meaningful-available-for, and this availability constitutes the from...toward... structure of movement.

tensionEdges.text: Heidegger - Basic Concepts of Aristotelian Philosophy
tensionEdges.description: Conceptuality has a 'double sense' precisely because the same λόγος that discloses also conceals. The fore-structures must be both overcome and appropriated. This tension drives the entire Second Part.

tensionEdges.text: Heidegger - Basic Concepts of Aristotelian Philosophy
tensionEdges.description: Theoretical science arises from and against the background of δόξα. Science is the transformation, not the abolition, of everyday opinion.

tensionEdges.text: Heidegger - Basic Concepts of Aristotelian Philosophy
tensionEdges.description: Neither is simply more fundamental. They are equiprimordial (gleichursprünglich) -- anticipating BT's analysis of Rede, Befindlichkeit, and Verstehen as co-original existentialia.

tensionEdges.text: Heidegger - Basic Concepts of Aristotelian Philosophy
tensionEdges.nodeA: ἀρετή as μεσότης (the mean πρὸς ἡμᾶς)
tensionEdges.nodeB: ἀρετή as ἀκρότης (the highest with regard to the εὖ)
tensionEdges.description: The tension dissolves when μεσότης is understood as a way of being-composed (the 'how') rather than a quantitative midpoint. The mean is the extreme because it is the mode of being most genuinely related to the concrete situation (καιρός).

tensionEdges.text: Heidegger - Basic Concepts of Aristotelian Philosophy
tensionEdges.description: The non-parallelism shows that dispositions are not reactions to pre-given objects but disclosive modes of being-in-the-world. The gap between φοβερά and φόβος makes fear a finding-oneself rather than a causal response.

tensionEdges.text: Heidegger - The Fundamental Concepts of Metaphysics
tensionEdges.nodeB: animal does not have world (withheld from beings as beings)
tensionEdges.description: Heidegger leaves it as a productive impasse: poverty (Entbehrung) names exactly this 'having in not-having'.

tensionEdges.text: Heidegger - The Fundamental Concepts of Metaphysics
tensionEdges.description: The counter-move is the best access route to the phenomenon (methodological directive §22).

tensionEdges.text: Heidegger - The Fundamental Concepts of Metaphysics
tensionEdges.nodeA: engaged all evening, would deny boredom
tensionEdges.nodeB: was bored; boredom rose from Dasein itself
tensionEdges.description: The second form just is the coexistence of occupied surface and empty depth.

tensionEdges.text: Heidegger - The Fundamental Concepts of Metaphysics
tensionEdges.description: PROJECTED: the instruments measure different structural layers of one second-form episode (surface gaze occupied / depth attunement hollow); dissolves under FCM §§24-25.

tensionEdges.text: Heidegger - The Fundamental Concepts of Metaphysics
tensionEdges.description: PROJECTED: time-dilation is the depth (Hingehaltenheit) leaking through an occupied surface — the second-form signature a bipolar scale cannot hold.

tensionEdges.text: Heidegger - The Fundamental Concepts of Metaphysics
tensionEdges.nodeA: profound boredom discloses beings as a whole (Grundstimmung)
tensionEdges.nodeB: a 17-minute lab stimulus induces bounded boredom
tensionEdges.description: The bridge borrows FCM's structural grammar as a heuristic; 'third form' transfers as phenomenology (stillness, ceased search), not as metaphysical disclosure.

tensionEdges.text: Heidegger - The Fundamental Concepts of Metaphysics
tensionEdges.description: PROJECTED (weak analogy): immersion occupies the surface while educational depth stays hollow — second-form-shaped, but no time/boredom probe so non-load-bearing.

Withdrawal is not the enemy of disclosure but its enabling condition; the world's inexhaustibility (its always-exceeding what we make of it) ensures rhetoric is never finished, always preparatory, always calling for further attunement. Withdrawal grounds rhetoric's inexhaustibility.

Rickert does not eliminate subjectivity but reconceives it as emplaced and distributed, preventing ambient rhetoric from collapsing into undifferentiated flat ontology while insisting that agency is never solely human.

Attunement redefines rather than eliminates skilled practice: the rhetor is seized by the moment rather than seizing it, but this requires a cultivated receptivity (ear cleaning, trust in the moment) that is itself a form of non-sovereign expertise.

Networks are necessary but insufficient: they correctly grasp the ontological character of relationality, but ambience adds the immersive, osmotic, choric thickness that the network metaphor cannot provide, driving the move from Part 1 to Part 2.

Rickert harvests Burke for the richness of social drama and embodied rhetoric while correcting him with Heidegger's more radical decentering; together they establish that meaning inheres in the world but disagree on whether humans remain the gravitational center of language.

Technology is both the condition under which ambient rhetoric becomes visible and the principal obstacle to genuine dwelling; ambient rhetoric requires not anti-technology but a transformed relation to technology grounded in dwelling rather than efficiency.

Rickert needs both: Latour's concrete demonstrations of material persuasion and Heidegger's deeper ontological framework. Dingpolitik does not come first through extending politics but emerges from dwelling as attunement -- the political is grounded in the ontological.

tensionEdges.text: Von Uexkull - A Foray into the Worlds of Animals and Humans
tensionEdges.description: The subject is defined against mechanism, yet the Funktionskreis -- the core analytical unit -- employs mechanistic vocabulary (receptor, effector, reflex arc). Uexkuell reinterprets but never fully escapes the machine idiom.

tensionEdges.text: Von Uexkull - A Foray into the Worlds of Animals and Humans
tensionEdges.description: Uexkuell strips teleological goal-language from biology but replaces it with 'Nature's plan' -- a concept that smuggles purposiveness back in under a different name. 'Nature knows how to deal with difficulties' is itself anthropomorphic.

tensionEdges.text: Von Uexkull - A Foray into the Worlds of Animals and Humans
tensionEdges.description: The Theory of Meaning oscillates between constructivism (meaning is impressed by the subject) and pre-established harmony (the Komplement-Bauplan fit implies a prior design that the subject merely activates).

tensionEdges.text: Von Uexkull - A Foray into the Worlds of Animals and Humans
tensionEdges.description: The search image is simultaneously a perception image and its antagonist. Composed of the same materials (perception signs), it can erase the very perception image it resembles, making the boundary between subject-generated and stimulus-driven perception unstable.

tensionEdges.text: Von Uexkull - A Foray into the Worlds of Animals and Humans
tensionEdges.description: The magical environment contradicts the stimulus-response architecture of the Funktionskreis. Early chapters build the functional cycle on perception marks from external objects; the magical chapter shows perception images arising without any object -- a free production of the subject that the original schema cannot accommodate.

tensionEdges.text: Von Uexkull - A Foray into the Worlds of Animals and Humans
tensionEdges.description: Uexkuell's perspectivism declares Nature unknowable, yet the biologist who writes about tick and spider Umwelten implicitly occupies a meta-perspectival position. The reflexivity problem -- how the Umwelt theorist escapes his own Umwelt -- is never resolved.

tensionEdges.text: Von Uexkull - A Foray into the Worlds of Animals and Humans
tensionEdges.description: The Kompositionslehre replaces causal explanation with contrapuntal description but never clarifies the ontological status of the meaning rule. It is not a force, not a substance, not a causal chain -- yet governs embryogenesis, cross-species adaptation, and ecological composition. Musical metaphor does real work but risks substituting analogy for explanation.

tensionEdges.text: Von Uexkull - A Foray into the Worlds of Animals and Humans
tensionEdges.description: The concept of Bedeutungsduldung introduces radical passivity into a framework built on subject-constituted worlds. The fly in the spider's web and the plant being grazed are subjects whose Umwelt is violated by another subject's meaning-conferral. Active subject-constitution and passive meaning-sufferance coexist without reconciliation.

tensionEdges.text: Von Uexkull - A Foray into the Worlds of Animals and Humans
tensionEdges.description: Naturtechnik promises a science of compositional principles, yet its central object -- the formative melody -- is declared inscrutable. The genes are keys, the protoplasm is material, but the melody that plays upon them is invisible. This positions Uexkuell's biology between empirical science and avowed mystery.

tensionEdges.text: Von Uexkull - A Foray into the Worlds of Animals and Humans
tensionEdges.description: The anti-Darwinian stance and the Kompositionslehre share the same evidential base -- mutual organism-environment fitness -- but interpret it oppositely. Darwin sees emergent adaptation through selection; Uexkuell sees pre-composed contrapuntal harmony. The choice between them cannot be settled by the examples alone.

tensionEdges.nodeA: POSITION:HR-01-GROSS-A-P2 (rhetoric relocated at heart of fundamental ontology)
tensionEdges.nodeB: POSITION:HR-07-POGGELER-P1 (rhetoric restricted to Marburg 1923-28; topology of being supplants)
tensionEdges.description: The volume's most architectural disagreement: Gross opens with the centrality thesis; Pöggeler closes with the restriction thesis. Hyde, Struever, Kisiel align with Gross on SS 1924 → BT continuity; Gadamer partially affirms (continuity through Befindlichkeit + late-restriction in poetics-only turn); Michalski's philological framing is methodologically sustaining (compatible with Gross's continuity). Gross-B-P10 (HR-01-GROSS-B-T4) reads Pöggeler's restriction-thesis as itself a *symptom* explained by Gross's depoliticization-by-hermeneutics diagnosis — Pöggeler reads late Heidegger and finds rhetoric restricted; Gross reads early Heidegger and explains why late Heidegger looks restricted. The disagreement is generative: each side exposes what the other underplays.

tensionEdges.nodeA: POSITION:HR-02-GADAMER-P1 + HR-05-STRUEVER-P3 + HR-06-KISIEL-P1 (rhetoric is dynamis, not technē)
tensionEdges.nodeB: Implicit: Aristotle's own elsewhere-designation of rhetoric as technē + post-Aristotelian rhetorical-instructional tradition
tensionEdges.description: Three contributors converge on the volume's central Aristotelian-philological commitment. Gadamer's interview is the locus classicus (Ch 2 §II response p. 49). Struever specifies dynamis tou theoresai (Rhet. 1355b26 / GA 18 122) — narrowing Gadamer's broader dynamis-claim to the specific textual anchor. Kisiel: rhetoric is 'first of all not an art but a power, dynamis ... cultivated power of situational insight, phronesis' (p. 146). Gadamer adds a subtle correction (HR-02-GADAMER-T4): 'Heidegger ... began emphatically using the concept of energeia. And so he associated the concept of dynamis with the concept of energeia, and missed the other one' — i.e., the productive-poietic dimension of technē was lost in the dynamis-energeia coupling. The volume's signature Aristotelian commitment is also its most-finely-graded.

tensionEdges.nodeA: Continuity-readings: HR-01-GROSS, HR-04-HYDE, HR-05-STRUEVER, HR-02-GADAMER (qualified), HR-03-MICHALSKI
tensionEdges.nodeB: Rupture/Restriction-readings: HR-07-POGGELER (rhetoric restricted to Marburg; topology of being is the post-1947 succession); HR-06-KISIEL (three-phase model: only Phase 1 is rhetorical)
tensionEdges.description: The volume contains three reading directions. Forward-readers (Gross, Hyde, Struever) trace 1924 → BT 1927 with substantive continuity; the move 'colonizes' BT from within (Struever) or constitutes its rhetorical genealogy (Gross). Backward-readers (Pöggeler) track 1947 → 1957 → Marburg → final position, finding the topology of being supplants rhetoric. Kisiel's three-phase model (1923-25 Phenomenological-rhetorical / 1933-35 Metontological-Führer / 1935-43 Archaic-Poietic-polemos) is the most articulated middle: rhetoric is restricted to Phase 1 (agreement with Pöggeler) but the *arc* of restriction is itself politically diagnostic (agreement with Gross's depoliticization thesis). Gadamer occupies a 'continuity-with-late-restriction' position — continuous through Befindlichkeit/Mitsein but acknowledges Heidegger's poetics-only turn was 'his weakest area' (Ch 2 p. 56).

tensionEdges.nodeA: Protopolitical reading: HR-06-KISIEL-P1 (rhetorical protopolitics, 1923-24 with Arendtian afterlife); HR-05-STRUEVER-P9 (Heideggerian politics of time briefly in SS 1924); HR-01-GROSS-B-P7 (rhetorical pluralism of 1924)
tensionEdges.nodeB: Depoliticization → tragedy: HR-01-GROSS-B-P9, P10 (1933 Nazism as political consequence of BT-era depoliticization); HR-04-HYDE-P7 (Heidegger's 1949 'agriculture/extermination' equation correlates with missing rhetoric's ontological status)
tensionEdges.description: Three contributors with distinct accounts of the rhetoric/politics relation; Kisiel's three-phase table on book p. 149 is the most articulated single position. Gross's diagnosis (Gross-B-P10 supports Gross-B-P9) is causal: the hermeneutic turn that depoliticized rhetoric also predisposed Heidegger to mistake propaganda-pathos for civic-pathos. Kisiel's diagnosis (HR-06-KISIEL-P3) is operational: Heidegger applied Aristotelian phronesis to the propaganda-political situation he himself had diagnosed in 1924. The two diagnoses are mutually reinforcing (per HR-06-KISIEL-T8-cross). Pöggeler's relative silence on the Nazi years is itself a position: the topology of being supplants both rhetoric AND politics.

tensionEdges.nodeA: POSITION:HR-04-HYDE-P1 (pathē as deliberate rhetorical resources for the orator; call of conscience operates 'ontologically as a primordial and emotional form of epideictic rhetoric'; orator's intentional structure preserved)
tensionEdges.nodeB: POSITION:HR-01-GROSS-B-P1 (pathos as ontological substrate — 'the very substance in which propositional thought finds its objects and motivation', Intro p. 4; orator dissolved into pre-cognitive Befindlichkeit)
tensionEdges.description: Six contributors stake distinct readings. Gadamer occupies a productive middle (HR-02-GADAMER-T6): pathē are pre-articulate ground (Gross-side) but also bewährt grounds-for-judgment (Hyde-side); the bewährt caveat is the volume's most philosophically careful navigation. Struever reads pathē as 'Befindlichkeiten oriented to others' (GA 18 207, 232) — intrinsically social-interpersonal, supporting Gross. Kisiel's pisteis-equiprimordial-with-aletheia reading (HR-06-KISIEL-P7) is more ontological than Hyde's, building on Gross. Pöggeler's diagnosis (HR-07-POGGELER-P2) is the negative case: Heidegger's gloss pathos = Befindlichkeit IS the moment of restriction — neither cognitive-resource nor ontological-substrate is preserved but rather dissolved into existential attunement.

tensionEdges.nodeA: POSITION:HR-01-GROSS-A-P3 (displacement entails 'political and ethical loss'; rhetoric depoliticized in hermeneutic turn; Gadamer 'downplays' the loss)
tensionEdges.nodeB: POSITION:HR-02-GADAMER-P7 (Sprachlichkeit / 'rhetoric is the overarching concept for everything that has to do with the other' — hermeneutics IS rhetoric properly understood, conceptually coextensive)
tensionEdges.description: Per HR-02-GADAMER-T7: Gadamer's position is more nuanced than Gross suggests. At the conceptual level, rhetoric and hermeneutics are coextensive ('It is the same dynamis!', Ch 2 p. 60); at the institutional-pedagogical level, Gadamer admits he never developed a rhetoric pedagogy and that this was a real limitation. Direct intra-volume engagement: Gross's Ch 1 critique is met by Gadamer's Ch 2 interview position. Gross's depoliticization-by-hermeneutics thesis (HR-01-GROSS-B-P10) extends the critique structurally — the 'sweep' of power into discursive backgrounds is a 20th-century outsourcing of rhetorical responsibility to speech-act theory (Searle, Grice, Habermas, Sperber).

tensionEdges.nodeA: POSITION:HR-03-MICHALSKI-P5 (philology is a NECESSARY ELEMENT of hermeneutic phenomenology; Heidegger 'explicitly rejects the title of philosophy in favor of philology even for the region exceeding the horizon of classical philology')
tensionEdges.nodeB: Implicit critique from HR-06-KISIEL who treats GA 18 as primarily *political* genesis text, not philological exercise
tensionEdges.description: Michalski (Ch 3) answers the titular question synthetically: phenomenology is hermeneuticized; hermeneutic phenomenology requires the philological moment; and philology in this enlarged sense IS the existentially-ontologically grounded directive of scientific research. Kisiel's protopolitical reading does not contradict this directly but draws different categorial consequences from the same loci. Pöggeler agrees with Michalski's philological framing but restricts the import (HR-07-POGGELER-P3 refines HR-03-MICHALSKI-P1): for Michalski the philological orientation is methodologically sustaining; for Pöggeler it's part of what makes the Marburg engagement a bounded episode.

tensionEdges.nodeA: POSITION:HR-05-STRUEVER-P2 (Alltäglichkeit = timefulness, the catalytic agent of temporality, solvent of eternity); aligned with Gross/Hyde/Kisiel readings of BT 178 as load-bearing positive endorsement
tensionEdges.nodeB: POSITION:HR-07-POGGELER-P7 (BT §29 reads Aristotle's Rhetoric as 'first systematic hermeneutic of everydayness' as RESTRICTION — Heidegger confines the political to everydayness/das Man, surrendering the deliberative-public dimension)
tensionEdges.description: Hyde takes BT 178 as positive Heidegger acknowledgment (Ch 4 p. 83); Pöggeler reads BT 178 as a momentary acknowledgment soon abandoned (Ch 7 p. 171). Kisiel reads it as constitutive for SS 1924 protopolitics (Ch 6 p. 132). Struever's titular coining ('timefulness') is the volume's most articulated alternative to the Blattner erosion-into-ordinariness thesis. Pöggeler's reading is structurally distinctive: not contesting the translation but reading the same passage as restrictive rather than constitutive — the political dimension is confined to everydayness/das Man, surrendering rhetoric's deliberative-public scope.

tensionEdges.nodeA: Gross, Struever, Hyde, Kisiel, Michalski all foreground GA 18 110 ('Rhetorik ist nichts anderes als die Auslegung des konkreten Daseins, die Hermeneutik des Daseins selbst') as the volume's most-cited single passage; load-bearing positive endorsement of rhetoric's centrality
tensionEdges.nodeB: Pöggeler does NOT foreground GA 18 110 (the absence is itself significant per HR-07-POGGELER-T2 and Phase 0 VT9); instead reads BT §29 (which contains substantively similar content) as the moment of restriction
tensionEdges.description: The architectural disagreement of VT1 is partially executed at the level of which Heidegger-quotations the contributors foreground. Pöggeler's contrastive omission of the GA 18 110 epigraph is itself a position (Phase 0 §7): the passage that Gross uses as epigraph and Struever uses as titular epigraph is structurally absent from Pöggeler's counterthesis. Pöggeler's implicit position (HR-07-POGGELER-P7): BT §29 + GA 18 110 is the moment Heidegger CONFINES the political to everydayness (das Man), thereby surrendering the deliberative-public dimension Aristotle's Rhetoric had named.

tensionEdges.nodeA: BCAP unit U-FP3a (GA 18 §§13-14): Heidegger's reading centers DELIBERATIVE rhetoric (sumbouleutikon) — practical deliberation (Beratung, krisis) about future action
tensionEdges.nodeB: POSITION:HR-04-HYDE-P1 (epideictic emphasis: BT call of conscience is primordial-ontological EPIDEICTIC, not deliberative)
tensionEdges.description: Hyde's reading EXTENDS Heidegger via Aristotle's typology while remaining textually constrained by Heidegger's actual emphases. Volume tension VT10 is therefore productive: BCAP unit U-FP3a's deliberative reading and Hyde's epideictic reading are both textually grounded but emphasize different Aristotelian genres. Kisiel (HR-06-KISIEL-T10-cross) adds a third rhetorical-genre register: ethos = Entschlossenheit (deliberative-political SZ §60), contrasting with Hyde's ethos = Ruf des Gewissens (epideictic-existential SZ §§54-60). The three readings (deliberative-BCAP, epideictic-Hyde, deliberative-Kisiel) make the BT call-of-conscience block a multi-genre rhetorical event in Phase 4.

tensionEdges.nodeA: BT pipeline unit BT-D1-U5 records Befindlichkeit (§29) + Furcht (§30) as canonical BT existentialia; these terms are the BT-authoritative renderings
tensionEdges.nodeB: POSITION:HR-01-GROSS-B-P1, P8 (pathos does conceptual work BT slightly conceals with the term Befindlichkeit; BT 344 / BT 434 document the substantive narrowing)
tensionEdges.description: Phase 3D cross-link required: BT pipeline + HR pipeline both treat Befindlichkeit as the institutionalized form of the SS 1924 pathos. The productive cross-pipeline question is whether the institutionalization preserves the substantive content. Gross-B argues no (BT 344 + BT 434 narrow Mitsein into individual resoluteness); Pöggeler agrees but reads as restriction; Michalski's editorial framing is methodologically sustaining (philology-as-hermeneutic-phenomenology preserves the GA 18 register). The cross-pipeline tension is generative for Phase 4 reconciliation.

tensionEdges.nodeA: Aristotle pipeline reads kinēsis (Phys. III.1-3, esp. 202b23) as ontologically primary; Met. IX (energeia/dynamis pairing)
tensionEdges.nodeB: HR-06-KISIEL reads Heidegger's SS 1924 kinēsis as politically charged (Heidegger's reading of GA 18 §§25-28 with poiētikon-pathētikon as conceptual track for BT poiesis-emphasis); HR-01-GROSS-A reads the same loci through the German middle voice as ontological-stylistic experiment (Intro pp. 20-22, Phys 202b23); HR-05-STRUEVER reads kinesis as the vital motion of life — 'If life, then motion, kinēsis. If motion, then time'
tensionEdges.description: Multi-way reading ripe for Phase 4. Aristotle pipeline's existing PHYS-03 unit needs to be enriched by the three HR readings: Kisiel's protopolitical kinēsis (GA 18 §§25-28 reads political-rhetorically); Gross's middle-voice kinēsis (Phys 202b23 read German-stylistically); Struever's life-temporal kinēsis (the syllogism 'life → motion → time'). Michalski's note 8 catalogs Heidegger's three approaches to kinēsis at Physics III.1-3 (GA 18 287f, 316, 323f) with Themistius/Simplicius commentaries — providing the philological scaffolding. The three readings are mutually enriching, not contradictory; Phase 4 cross-link should preserve the four-way structure (Aristotle / Gross / Struever / Kisiel).
